181	def level_candidates(d_on, cov, controls, n, n_max, realisable, all_only=False, bases=("Z", "X")):
182	    """[(n_removed, mask, basis, control set, Flag)], best coverage first, only
183	    control sets with a Willow embedding (``realisable(qs, basis)``), each
184	    concrete flag (probe set) once."""
185	    out = []
186	    full_mask = (1 << n) - 1
187	    for basis in bases:
188	        for qs in control_sets(d_on, controls):
189	            cols = [k for k, p in enumerate(cov.pa.probes) if p.q in qs and p.basis == basis]
190	            if not cols:
191	                continue
192	            if all_only:
193	                masks = [full_mask] if Z.solve_gf2(cov.system(cols, list(range(n))), len(cols)) else []
194	            elif n <= 10:
195	                masks = maximal(Z.coverable_subsets(cov, cols, n))
196	            else:
197	                masks = maximal(greedy_masks(cov, cols, n))
198	            for m in masks:
199	                out.append((bin(m).count("1"), m, basis, qs, cols))
200	    out.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[0], x[2] != "Z", len(x[3])))
201	    res, seen = [], set()
202	    mid = d_on.mid_ticks[0] if d_on.mid_ticks else 10 ** 9
203	    for k, m, basis, qs, cols in out:
204	        if realisable is not None and not realisable(qs, basis == "X"):
205	            continue   # not even with the flag dormant at the mid check
206	        for fl in Z.concrete_flags(cov, cols, [i for i in range(n) if m >> i & 1], limit=4):
207	            live = basis == "X" or min(p.slot for p in fl.probes) <= mid
208	            if fl.probes in seen or (realisable is not None and not realisable(qs, live)):
209	                continue
210	            seen.add(fl.probes)
211	            res.append((k, m, basis, qs, fl))
212	        if len(res) >= n_max:
213	            break
214	    return res[:n_max]
215	
216	
217	def realisability(d, specs):
218	    cache = {}
219	
220	    def f(qs, live):
221	        key = (qs, live)
222	        if key not in cache:
223	            cache[key] = next(Z.embeddings(d, list(specs) + [(qs, live)]), None) is not None
224	        return cache[key]
225	    return None if specs is None else f
226	
227	
228	def process(task):
229	    """Worker: full two/three-level search on one base."""
230	    name, key, entry, opts = task
231	    t0 = time.perf_counter()
232	    info = dict(base=name)
233	    try:
234	        d = Z.design_g4() if key == "G4" else Z.design_from_option1(key, entry, name=name)
235	        tree_q = list(d.qubits)
236	        pa = Z.ProbeAnalysis(d, controls=tree_q)
237	        pairs, events, _, _ = Z.malignant_pairs(d)
238	        d.info["T2"] = len(pairs)
239	        n = len(pairs)
240	        cov = Z.Coverage(pa, pairs, events)
241	        ev = Evaluator(d, name)
242	        info.update(base_T2=n, tree=d.info.get("tree"), labelling=str(d.info.get("lab", "")),
243	                    n_pairs=n, pairs=json.dumps(pairs))
244	        real1 = realisability(d, [])
245	        filt = None if opts.get("abstract") else real1
246	        # coverage evidence: which pairs some single (basis, control set) flag can separate,
247	        # and which of those control sets have a Willow embedding
248	        sep, sep_real = defaultdict(int), defaultdict(int)
249	        for basis in ("Z", "X"):
250	            for qs in control_sets(d, tree_q):
251	                cols = [k for k, p in enumerate(pa.probes) if p.q in qs and p.basis == basis]
252	                for i in range(n):
253	                    if Z.solve_gf2(cov.system(cols, [i]), len(cols)) is not None:
254	                        sep[i] += 1
255	                        sep_real[i] += real1(qs, basis == "X")
256	        info["single_flag_separable"] = json.dumps({i: [sep[i], sep_real[i]] for i in range(n)})
257	        info["unseparable_pairs"] = json.dumps(dict(
258	            any_control_set=[pairs[i] for i in range(n) if not sep[i]],
259	            realisable_control_set=[pairs[i] for i in range(n) if not sep_real[i]]))
260	        info["pair_hooks"] = json.dumps({str(pairs[i]): [hook_text(pa, events, f, d.nq) for f in pairs[i]]
261	                                         for i in range(n)})
262	        # level 1
263	        lvl = defaultdict(list)
264	        for k, m, basis, qs, fl in level_candidates(d, cov, tree_q, n, opts["n1"], filt, bases=opts["bases"]):
265	            r = ev.evaluate(d, [fl], 1, k)
266	            if r:
267	                lvl[1].append((r[2]["malignant_T_2"], r[2]["ler_T_mfc2"], r[2]["realisable"], r[0], r[1]))
268	        info["best_level1_T2"] = min((x[0] for x in lvl[1] if x[2]), default="")
269	        frontier = sorted([x for x in lvl[1] if x[2] and x[0] > 0], key=lambda x: (x[0], x[1]))[:opts["k1"]]
270	        for level in range(2, opts["max_flags"] + 1):
271	            for _, _, _, inner, fq in frontier:
272	                if len(ev.success) >= opts["stop_per_base"]:
273	                    break
274	                d1 = Z.Design(name + f"+L{level - 1}", inner, d.full_args, {}, info=d.info)
275	                pa1 = Z.ProbeAnalysis(d1, controls=tree_q)
276	                pairs1, events1, _, _ = Z.malignant_pairs(d1)
277	                if not pairs1:
278	                    continue
279	                cov1 = Z.Coverage(pa1, pairs1, events1)
280	                n1 = len(pairs1)
281	                real = realisability(d, None if opts.get("abstract") else Z.flag_specs(inner, fq)[0])
282	                c2 = level_candidates(d1, cov1, tree_q, n1, opts["n2"], real, all_only=True, bases=opts["bases"])
283	                if not c2:   # no flag removes all: record / extend the best partial coverages
284	                    c2 = level_candidates(d1, cov1, tree_q, n1,
285	                                          opts["n2_partial"] if level < opts["max_flags"] else 2, real,
286	                                          bases=opts["bases"])
287	                for k, m, basis, qs, fl in c2:
288	                    r = ev.evaluate(d1, [fl], level, k, extra_fq=fq)
289	                    if r:
290	                        lvl[level].append((r[2]["malignant_T_2"], r[2]["ler_T_mfc2"], r[2]["realisable"],
291	                                           r[0], r[1]))
292	            info[f"best_level{level}_T2"] = min((x[0] for x in lvl[level] if x[2]), default="")
293	            frontier = sorted([x for x in lvl[level] if x[2] and x[0] > 0],
294	                              key=lambda x: (x[0], x[1]))[:opts["k1"]]
295	        info.update(n_evaluated=len(ev.rows), n_success=len(ev.success))
296	        info["seconds"] = round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 1)
297	        return info, ev.rows, ev.success, ev.best
298	    except Exception as e:  # keep the run alive; record the error
299	        info.update(error=f"{type(e).__name__}: {e} | {traceback.format_exc()[-600:]}",
300	                    seconds=round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 1))
301	        return info, [], [], []
302	
303	
304	def tasks(opts, limit=None):
305	    screen = json.loads(SCREEN.read_text())
306	    keys = [k for k, v in screen.items() if min(int(x) for x in v["hist"]) < INFEASIBLE]
307	    keys.sort(key=lambda k: (min(int(x) for x in screen[k]["hist"]), screen[k]["rate"]))
308	    out = [("G4", "G4", None, opts)]
309	    for i, k in enumerate(keys[:limit]):
310	        out.append((f"B{i:04d}", k, screen[k], opts))
311	    return out
312	
313	
314	def main():
315	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
316	    ap.add_argument("--out", default="results")
317	    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=12)
318	    ap.add_argument("--max-flags", type=int, default=2)
319	    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=None, help="number of Option-1 bases")
320	    ap.add_argument("--hours", type=float, default=6.0)
321	    ap.add_argument("--n1", type=int, default=40)
322	    ap.add_argument("--k1", type=int, default=8)
323	    ap.add_argument("--n2", type=int, default=16)
324	    ap.add_argument("--n2-partial", type=int, default=6)
325	    ap.add_argument("--tag", default="zz")
326	    ap.add_argument("--abstract", action="store_true",
327	                    help="evidence pass: no Willow-realisability filter on the flags")
328	    ap.add_argument("--stop-per-base", type=int, default=2)
329	    ap.add_argument("--only-bases", default=None, help="file with base names (one per line) to run")
330	    ap.add_argument("--bases", default="ZX", help="flag families: Z (generalised Z flags), X, or ZX")
331	    args = ap.parse_args()
332	    out = Path(args.out)
333	    sdir = out / args.tag
334	    sdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
335	    opts = dict(max_flags=args.max_flags, n1=args.n1, k1=args.k1, n2=args.n2,
336	                n2_partial=args.n2_partial, stop_per_base=args.stop_per_base,
337	                abstract=args.abstract, bases=tuple(args.bases))
338	    t0 = time.time()
339	    log = lambda *a: print(f"[{time.time() - t0:8.1f} s]", *a, flush=True)
340	    todo = tasks(opts, args.limit)
341	    if args.only_bases:
342	        keep = set(Path(args.only_bases).read_text().split())
343	        todo = [t for t in todo if t[0] in keep]
344	    log(f"{len(todo)} bases queued (G4 + {len(todo) - 1} Option-1 bases), opts {opts}")
345	    suffix = "" if args.tag == "zz" else "_" + args.tag.removeprefix("zz_")
346	    fh = (out / f"zz_candidates{suffix}.csv").open("w", newline="")
347	    wr = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=FIELDS, extrasaction="ignore")
348	    wr.writeheader()
349	    bh = (out / f"zz_bases{suffix}.csv").open("w", newline="")
350	    bw = csv.DictWriter(bh, fieldnames=BASE_FIELDS, extrasaction="ignore")
351	    bw.writeheader()
352	    state = dict(settings=dict(args=vars(args), noise="uniformly_depolarize", p=Z.NOISE,
353	                               max_fault_count=[2, 3], readout="strict", live_rule="gate",
354	                               final_layer="auto", max_degree=4), started=time.ctime())
355	    nid = n_succ = n_bases = 0
356	    best_global = []
357	    stop_reason = "design space exhausted"
358	    with Pool(args.workers) as pool:
359	        for info, rows, succ, best in pool.imap(process, todo, chunksize=1):
360	            n_bases += 1
361	            for k, row in enumerate(rows):
362	                row["id"] = nid + k
363	            for idx, inner, full, emb in succ:
364	                i = n_succ
365	                row = rows[idx]
366	                p = sdir / f"success{i:02d}.inner.stim"
367	                p.write_text(inner)
368	                (sdir / f"success{i:02d}.full.stim").write_text(full)
369	                row.update(stim_file=str(p), full_stim_file=str(sdir / f"success{i:02d}.full.stim"))
370	                n_succ += 1
371	                log(f"SUCCESS #{i} base {info['base']} flags {row['flags']} T3={row.get('malignant_T_3')} "
372	                    f"S2={row['malignant_S_2']} LER 1 in {row['ler_T_mfc2_one_in']}")
373	            for t2, rate, idx, inner, full in best:
374	                best_global.append((t2, rate, rows[idx]["id"], info["base"], inner, full))
375	            best_global.sort(key=lambda x: (x[0], x[1]))
376	            del best_global[5:]
377	            for row in rows:
378	                wr.writerow(row)
379	            fh.flush()
380	            nid += len(rows)
381	            bw.writerow(info)
382	            bh.flush()
383	            log(f"base {info['base']} T2={info.get('base_T2')} eval={len(rows)} "
384	                f"L1={info.get('best_level1_T2')} L2={info.get('best_level2_T2')} "
385	                f"L3={info.get('best_level3_T2', '')} succ={len(succ)} {info.get('seconds')} s"
386	                + (f" ERROR {info['error'][:200]}" if info.get("error") else ""))
387	            if n_bases % 10 == 0 or succ:
388	                for k, (t2, rate, rid, b, inner, full) in enumerate(best_global):
389	                    (sdir / f"best{k}.inner.stim").write_text(inner)
390	                    (sdir / f"best{k}.full.stim").write_text(full)
391	                state.update(n_bases_done=n_bases, n_evaluated=nid, n_success=n_succ,
392	                             best_non_success=[dict(T2=t2, rate=rate, id=rid, base=b)
393	                                               for t2, rate, rid, b, _, _ in best_global],
394	                             elapsed_s=time.time() - t0)
395	                (out / f"{args.tag}_state.json").write_text(json.dumps(state, indent=1))
396	            if n_succ >= STOP_SUCCESSES:
397	                stop_reason = f"{STOP_SUCCESSES} successes"
398	                pool.terminate()
399	                break
400	            if time.time() - t0 > args.hours * 3600:
401	                stop_reason = f"time limit {args.hours} h"
402	                pool.terminate()
403	                break
404	    for k, (t2, rate, rid, b, inner, full) in enumerate(best_global):
405	        (sdir / f"best{k}.inner.stim").write_text(inner)
406	        (sdir / f"best{k}.full.stim").write_text(full)
407	    state.update(n_bases_done=n_bases, n_bases_queued=len(todo), n_evaluated=nid, n_success=n_succ,
408	                 stop_reason=stop_reason, finished=time.ctime(), elapsed_s=time.time() - t0,
409	                 best_non_success=[dict(T2=t2, rate=rate, id=rid, base=b)
410	                                   for t2, rate, rid, b, _, _ in best_global])
411	    (out / f"{args.tag}_state.json").write_text(json.dumps(state, indent=1))
412	    fh.close()
413	    bh.close()
414	    log("done:", stop_reason, f"bases {n_bases}, evaluated {nid}, successes {n_succ}")
415	
416	
417	if __name__ == "__main__":
418	    main()

"""ZZ-flag round: generalised Z / X flags (zzflags.py) on G4-type fold trees.

DESIGN SPACE
  * Bases: G4's extracted double check (CX form, results/g4/G4-CX.inner.stim)
    and the feasible abstract fold forests of the Option-1 screen
    (results/option1_screen.json, best code labelling per base), in order of
    best malignant 2-fault T count (then base rate).
  * Flags: generalised Z flags (R f, CX q_i -> f at chosen slots, M f in the
    final layer + DETECTOR) and, as the secondary family, X flags (RX f,
    CX f -> q_i, MX f). Controls of one flag: 1-4 tree qubits of the same grid
    colour (depth parity), each with tree degree <= 3 (it needs a free grid
    neighbour). Slots: existing TICKs where the control is idle, or new TICKs.
  * Two-level greedy search per base (exact prefilter, see zzflags.py):
      level 1: for every (basis, control set) every maximal set of malignant
               pairs one flag can remove; up to N1 concrete flags, best
               coverage first; each built, embedded (exists?) and verified;
      level 2: the K best realisable level-1 circuits become new bases (their
               own faults included exactly); a second flag must remove ALL
               their malignant pairs (else the best partial coverages are
               evaluated to record the best count reached).
      level 3 (--max-flags 3, the extra pass): same once more.
  * Every evaluated circuit gets verify(max_fault_count=2). Circuits with 0
    malignant T configurations at <= 2 faults ("successes") must also pass
    constraints.check_circuit (strict readout, live_rule="gate",
    final_layer="auto"; nearest-neighbour; degree <= 4; no reuse) under a Willow
    embedding, equivalence.check_equivalence (flags excluded from (iii)), and
    get verify(max_fault_count=3).

Usage: nohup .venv/bin/python -m nnflags.search_zzflags --workers 12 > logs/search_zzflags.log &
Outputs: results/zz_candidates.csv (every evaluated circuit), results/zz_bases.csv
(per base: pairs, coverage evidence), results/zz/*.stim, results/zz_state.json.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import itertools
import json
import time
import traceback
from collections import defaultdict
from multiprocessing import Pool
from pathlib import Path

from nnflags import constraints as C
from nnflags import equivalence as Q
from nnflags import zzflags as Z
from nnflags.verify import verify
from nnflags.willow import readout_line

SCREEN = Path("results/option1_screen.json")
INFEASIBLE = 10 ** 6
STOP_SUCCESSES = 10

FIELDS = ["id", "base", "base_T2", "level", "n_flags", "basis", "flags", "flag_controls",
          "flag_positions", "added_ticks", "n_qubits", "n_cx", "max_degree", "ticks",
          "predicted_removed", "malignant_T_1", "malignant_T_2", "malignant_S_2", "malignant_T_3",
          "ler_T_mfc2", "ler_T_mfc2_one_in", "ler_T_mfc3", "ler_T_mfc3_one_in",
          "realisable", "hardware_ok", "equivalence_ok", "success", "reason", "stim_file",
          "full_stim_file", "runtime_s"]
BASE_FIELDS = ["base", "base_T2", "tree", "labelling", "n_pairs", "pairs", "pair_hooks",
               "single_flag_separable", "unseparable_pairs", "best_level1_T2", "best_level2_T2",
               "best_level3_T2", "n_evaluated", "n_success", "seconds", "error"]


# ---- helpers ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def control_sets(d: Z.Design, controls, maxsize=4):
    deg = {q: len(d.adj.get(q, ())) for q in controls}
    ok = [q for q in controls if deg[q] <= 3]
    out = []
    for size in range(1, maxsize + 1):
        for qs in itertools.combinations(ok, size):
            if len({d.colour[q] for q in qs}) == 1:
                out.append(qs)
    return out


def maximal(masks):
    return [m for m in masks if not any(o != m and o & m == m for o in masks)]


def greedy_masks(cov, cols, n):
    """Large pair counts: grow one mask greedily from every single coverable pair."""
    single = [i for i in range(n) if Z.solve_gf2(cov.system(cols, [i]), len(cols)) is not None]
    out = set()
    for s in single:
        cur = [s]
        for i in single:
            if i not in cur and Z.solve_gf2(cov.system(cols, cur + [i]), len(cols)) is not None:
                cur.append(i)
        out.add(sum(1 << i for i in cur))
    return sorted(out)


def flag_description(inner, fq):
    specs, gates = Z.flag_specs(inner, fq)
    parts = []
    for f in fq:
        g = sorted(gates[f])
        parts.append(f"{g[0][2]}f{f}[" + "+".join(f"q{q}@t{t}" for t, q, _ in g) + "]")
    return ";".join(parts), specs, gates


def hook_text(pa, events, i, nq):
    """Short text of a fault class: its events (tick: Pauli)."""
    evs = sorted({(t, str(ps)[1:].replace("_", "")) for t, ps in events[i]})
    return f"#{i}:" + ",".join(f"t{t}" for t, _ in evs[:4]) + ("…" if len(evs) > 4 else "")


class Evaluator:
    """Builds, embeds and verifies flagged circuits of one base."""

    def __init__(self, base: Z.Design, name):
        self.base = base
        self.name = name
        self.rows = []
        self.success = []
        self.best = []   # (T2, row, inner text, full text) of realisable non-successes

    def evaluate(self, d_on: Z.Design, flags, level, predicted, extra_fq=()):
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        row = dict(base=self.name, base_T2=self.base.info.get("T2"), level=level,
                   predicted_removed=predicted)
        try:
            inner, fq_new = Z.build_flagged(d_on, flags)
        except ValueError as e:
            row.update(reason=f"build: {e}", n_flags=len(extra_fq) + len(flags),
                       flags=";".join(map(str, flags)))
            self.rows.append(row)
            return None
        fq = list(extra_fq) + list(fq_new)
        desc, specs, gates = flag_description(inner, fq)
        row.update(n_flags=len(fq), basis="".join(sorted({s for f in fq for _, _, s in gates[f]})),
                   flags=desc, flag_controls=json.dumps([list(s[0]) for s in specs]),
                   added_ticks=len(Q.to_layers(inner)) - self.base.T,
                   n_qubits=inner.num_qubits, n_cx=len(C.two_qubit_gates(inner)),
                   max_degree=max(map(len, C.partners(inner).values())), ticks=inner.num_ticks)
        emb = next(Z.embeddings(self.base, specs), None)
        row["realisable"] = emb is not None
        full = self.base.full(inner)
        r2 = verify(full, inner, max_fault_count=2)
        row.update(malignant_T_1=r2["T"][1]["malignant"], malignant_T_2=r2["T"][2]["malignant"],
                   malignant_S_2=r2["S"][2]["malignant"] + r2["S"][1]["malignant"],
                   ler_T_mfc2=r2["error_rate_per_kept_shot"]["T"])
        rate = row["ler_T_mfc2"]
        row["ler_T_mfc2_one_in"] = round(1 / rate) if rate > 0 else ""
        ok_fd3 = row["malignant_T_1"] == 0 and row["malignant_T_2"] == 0
        if emb is not None and ok_fd3:
            self._validate(row, inner, full, fq, specs)
        elif emb is None:
            row["reason"] = "no Willow embedding (tree + flag points)"
        row["runtime_s"] = round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 3)
        self.rows.append(row)
        if emb is not None and not row.get("success"):
            self.best.append((row["malignant_T_2"], row["ler_T_mfc2"], len(self.rows) - 1,
                              str(inner), str(full)))
            self.best.sort(key=lambda x: (x[0], x[1]))
            del self.best[3:]
        return inner, fq, row

    def _validate(self, row, inner, full, fq, specs):
        emb, tried, last = Z.find_valid_embedding(self.base, specs, inner)
        row["hardware_ok"] = emb is not None
        if emb is None:
            row["reason"] = f"hardware: {tried} embeddings tried, last {json.dumps(C.summarize(last or []))}"
            return
        eq = Q.check_equivalence(inner, full, flag_qubits=tuple(fq))
        row["equivalence_ok"] = eq["ok"]
        if not eq["ok"]:
            row["reason"] = "equivalence: " + json.dumps(
                {k: eq[k]["ok"] for k in ("i_code", "ii_check", "iii_reverse", "iv_deterministic")})
            return
        r3 = verify(full, inner, max_fault_count=3)
        rate3 = r3["error_rate_per_kept_shot"]["T"]
        row.update(malignant_T_3=r3["T"][3]["malignant"], ler_T_mfc3=rate3,
                   ler_T_mfc3_one_in=round(1 / rate3) if rate3 > 0 else "",
                   flag_positions=json.dumps({f: emb[f] for f in fq}), success=True)
        head = "\n".join(f"QUBIT_COORDS({emb[q][0]}, {emb[q][1]}) {q}" for q in sorted(emb))
        self.success.append((len(self.rows), head + "\n" + str(inner), str(full), emb))


def level_candidates(d_on, cov, controls, n, n_max, realisable, all_only=False, bases=("Z", "X")):
    """[(n_removed, mask, basis, control set, Flag)], best coverage first, only
    control sets with a Willow embedding (``realisable(qs, basis)``), each
    concrete flag (probe set) once."""
    out = []
    full_mask = (1 << n) - 1
    for basis in bases:
        for qs in control_sets(d_on, controls):
            cols = [k for k, p in enumerate(cov.pa.probes) if p.q in qs and p.basis == basis]
            if not cols:
                continue
            if all_only:
                masks = [full_mask] if Z.solve_gf2(cov.system(cols, list(range(n))), len(cols)) else []
            elif n <= 10:
                masks = maximal(Z.coverable_subsets(cov, cols, n))
            else:
                masks = maximal(greedy_masks(cov, cols, n))
            for m in masks:
                out.append((bin(m).count("1"), m, basis, qs, cols))
    out.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[0], x[2] != "Z", len(x[3])))
    res, seen = [], set()
    mid = d_on.mid_ticks[0] if d_on.mid_ticks else 10 ** 9
    for k, m, basis, qs, cols in out:
        if realisable is not None and not realisable(qs, basis == "X"):
            continue   # not even with the flag dormant at the mid check
        for fl in Z.concrete_flags(cov, cols, [i for i in range(n) if m >> i & 1], limit=4):
            live = basis == "X" or min(p.slot for p in fl.probes) <= mid
            if fl.probes in seen or (realisable is not None and not realisable(qs, live)):
                continue
            seen.add(fl.probes)
            res.append((k, m, basis, qs, fl))
        if len(res) >= n_max:
            break
    return res[:n_max]


def realisability(d, specs):
    cache = {}

    def f(qs, live):
        key = (qs, live)
        if key not in cache:
            cache[key] = next(Z.embeddings(d, list(specs) + [(qs, live)]), None) is not None
        return cache[key]
    return None if specs is None else f


def process(task):
    """Worker: full two/three-level search on one base."""
    name, key, entry, opts = task
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    info = dict(base=name)
    try:
        d = Z.design_g4() if key == "G4" else Z.design_from_option1(key, entry, name=name)
        tree_q = list(d.qubits)
        pa = Z.ProbeAnalysis(d, controls=tree_q)
        pairs, events, _, _ = Z.malignant_pairs(d)
        d.info["T2"] = len(pairs)
        n = len(pairs)
        cov = Z.Coverage(pa, pairs, events)
        ev = Evaluator(d, name)
        info.update(base_T2=n, tree=d.info.get("tree"), labelling=str(d.info.get("lab", "")),
                    n_pairs=n, pairs=json.dumps(pairs))
        real1 = realisability(d, [])
        filt = None if opts.get("abstract") else real1
        # coverage evidence: which pairs some single (basis, control set) flag can separate,
        # and which of those control sets have a Willow embedding
        sep, sep_real = defaultdict(int), defaultdict(int)
        for basis in ("Z", "X"):
            for qs in control_sets(d, tree_q):
                cols = [k for k, p in enumerate(pa.probes) if p.q in qs and p.basis == basis]
                for i in range(n):
                    if Z.solve_gf2(cov.system(cols, [i]), len(cols)) is not None:
                        sep[i] += 1
                        sep_real[i] += real1(qs, basis == "X")
        info["single_flag_separable"] = json.dumps({i: [sep[i], sep_real[i]] for i in range(n)})
        info["unseparable_pairs"] = json.dumps(dict(
            any_control_set=[pairs[i] for i in range(n) if not sep[i]],
            realisable_control_set=[pairs[i] for i in range(n) if not sep_real[i]]))
        info["pair_hooks"] = json.dumps({str(pairs[i]): [hook_text(pa, events, f, d.nq) for f in pairs[i]]
                                         for i in range(n)})
        # level 1
        lvl = defaultdict(list)
        for k, m, basis, qs, fl in level_candidates(d, cov, tree_q, n, opts["n1"], filt, bases=opts["bases"]):
            r = ev.evaluate(d, [fl], 1, k)
            if r:
                lvl[1].append((r[2]["malignant_T_2"], r[2]["ler_T_mfc2"], r[2]["realisable"], r[0], r[1]))
        info["best_level1_T2"] = min((x[0] for x in lvl[1] if x[2]), default="")
        frontier = sorted([x for x in lvl[1] if x[2] and x[0] > 0], key=lambda x: (x[0], x[1]))[:opts["k1"]]
        for level in range(2, opts["max_flags"] + 1):
            for _, _, _, inner, fq in frontier:
                if len(ev.success) >= opts["stop_per_base"]:
                    break
                d1 = Z.Design(name + f"+L{level - 1}", inner, d.full_args, {}, info=d.info)
                pa1 = Z.ProbeAnalysis(d1, controls=tree_q)
                pairs1, events1, _, _ = Z.malignant_pairs(d1)
                if not pairs1:
                    continue
                cov1 = Z.Coverage(pa1, pairs1, events1)
                n1 = len(pairs1)
                real = realisability(d, None if opts.get("abstract") else Z.flag_specs(inner, fq)[0])
                c2 = level_candidates(d1, cov1, tree_q, n1, opts["n2"], real, all_only=True, bases=opts["bases"])
                if not c2:   # no flag removes all: record / extend the best partial coverages
                    c2 = level_candidates(d1, cov1, tree_q, n1,
                                          opts["n2_partial"] if level < opts["max_flags"] else 2, real,
                                          bases=opts["bases"])
                for k, m, basis, qs, fl in c2:
                    r = ev.evaluate(d1, [fl], level, k, extra_fq=fq)
                    if r:
                        lvl[level].append((r[2]["malignant_T_2"], r[2]["ler_T_mfc2"], r[2]["realisable"],
                                           r[0], r[1]))
            info[f"best_level{level}_T2"] = min((x[0] for x in lvl[level] if x[2]), default="")
            frontier = sorted([x for x in lvl[level] if x[2] and x[0] > 0],
                              key=lambda x: (x[0], x[1]))[:opts["k1"]]
        info.update(n_evaluated=len(ev.rows), n_success=len(ev.success))
        info["seconds"] = round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 1)
        return info, ev.rows, ev.success, ev.best
    except Exception as e:  # keep the run alive; record the error
        info.update(error=f"{type(e).__name__}: {e} | {traceback.format_exc()[-600:]}",
                    seconds=round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 1))
        return info, [], [], []


def tasks(opts, limit=None):
    screen = json.loads(SCREEN.read_text())
    keys = [k for k, v in screen.items() if min(int(x) for x in v["hist"]) < INFEASIBLE]
    keys.sort(key=lambda k: (min(int(x) for x in screen[k]["hist"]), screen[k]["rate"]))
    out = [("G4", "G4", None, opts)]
    for i, k in enumerate(keys[:limit]):
        out.append((f"B{i:04d}", k, screen[k], opts))
    return out


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="results")
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=12)
    ap.add_argument("--max-flags", type=int, default=2)
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=None, help="number of Option-1 bases")
    ap.add_argument("--hours", type=float, default=6.0)
    ap.add_argument("--n1", type=int, default=40)
    ap.add_argument("--k1", type=int, default=8)
    ap.add_argument("--n2", type=int, default=16)
    ap.add_argument("--n2-partial", type=int, default=6)
    ap.add_argument("--tag", default="zz")
    ap.add_argument("--abstract", action="store_true",
                    help="evidence pass: no Willow-realisability filter on the flags")
    ap.add_argument("--stop-per-base", type=int, default=2)
    ap.add_argument("--only-bases", default=None, help="file with base names (one per line) to run")
    ap.add_argument("--bases", default="ZX", help="flag families: Z (generalised Z flags), X, or ZX")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    out = Path(args.out)
    sdir = out / args.tag
    sdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    opts = dict(max_flags=args.max_flags, n1=args.n1, k1=args.k1, n2=args.n2,
                n2_partial=args.n2_partial, stop_per_base=args.stop_per_base,
                abstract=args.abstract, bases=tuple(args.bases))
    t0 = time.time()
    log = lambda *a: print(f"[{time.time() - t0:8.1f} s]", *a, flush=True)
    todo = tasks(opts, args.limit)
    if args.only_bases:
        keep = set(Path(args.only_bases).read_text().split())
        todo = [t for t in todo if t[0] in keep]
    log(f"{len(todo)} bases queued (G4 + {len(todo) - 1} Option-1 bases), opts {opts}")
    suffix = "" if args.tag == "zz" else "_" + args.tag.removeprefix("zz_")
    fh = (out / f"zz_candidates{suffix}.csv").open("w", newline="")
    wr = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=FIELDS, extrasaction="ignore")
    wr.writeheader()
    bh = (out / f"zz_bases{suffix}.csv").open("w", newline="")
    bw = csv.DictWriter(bh, fieldnames=BASE_FIELDS, extrasaction="ignore")
    bw.writeheader()
    state = dict(settings=dict(args=vars(args), noise="uniformly_depolarize", p=Z.NOISE,
                               max_fault_count=[2, 3], readout="strict", live_rule="gate",
                               final_layer="auto", max_degree=4), started=time.ctime())
    nid = n_succ = n_bases = 0
    best_global = []
    stop_reason = "design space exhausted"
    with Pool(args.workers) as pool:
        for info, rows, succ, best in pool.imap(process, todo, chunksize=1):
            n_bases += 1
            for k, row in enumerate(rows):
                row["id"] = nid + k
            for idx, inner, full, emb in succ:
                i = n_succ
                row = rows[idx]
                p = sdir / f"success{i:02d}.inner.stim"
                p.write_text(inner)
                (sdir / f"success{i:02d}.full.stim").write_text(full)
                row.update(stim_file=str(p), full_stim_file=str(sdir / f"success{i:02d}.full.stim"))
                n_succ += 1
                log(f"SUCCESS #{i} base {info['base']} flags {row['flags']} T3={row.get('malignant_T_3')} "
                    f"S2={row['malignant_S_2']} LER 1 in {row['ler_T_mfc2_one_in']}")
            for t2, rate, idx, inner, full in best:
                best_global.append((t2, rate, rows[idx]["id"], info["base"], inner, full))
            best_global.sort(key=lambda x: (x[0], x[1]))
            del best_global[5:]
            for row in rows:
                wr.writerow(row)
            fh.flush()
            nid += len(rows)
            bw.writerow(info)
            bh.flush()
            log(f"base {info['base']} T2={info.get('base_T2')} eval={len(rows)} "
                f"L1={info.get('best_level1_T2')} L2={info.get('best_level2_T2')} "
                f"L3={info.get('best_level3_T2', '')} succ={len(succ)} {info.get('seconds')} s"
                + (f" ERROR {info['error'][:200]}" if info.get("error") else ""))
            if n_bases % 10 == 0 or succ:
                for k, (t2, rate, rid, b, inner, full) in enumerate(best_global):
                    (sdir / f"best{k}.inner.stim").write_text(inner)
                    (sdir / f"best{k}.full.stim").write_text(full)
                state.update(n_bases_done=n_bases, n_evaluated=nid, n_success=n_succ,
                             best_non_success=[dict(T2=t2, rate=rate, id=rid, base=b)
                                               for t2, rate, rid, b, _, _ in best_global],
                             elapsed_s=time.time() - t0)
                (out / f"{args.tag}_state.json").write_text(json.dumps(state, indent=1))
            if n_succ >= STOP_SUCCESSES:
                stop_reason = f"{STOP_SUCCESSES} successes"
                pool.terminate()
                break
            if time.time() - t0 > args.hours * 3600:
                stop_reason = f"time limit {args.hours} h"
                pool.terminate()
                break
    for k, (t2, rate, rid, b, inner, full) in enumerate(best_global):
        (sdir / f"best{k}.inner.stim").write_text(inner)
        (sdir / f"best{k}.full.stim").write_text(full)
    state.update(n_bases_done=n_bases, n_bases_queued=len(todo), n_evaluated=nid, n_success=n_succ,
                 stop_reason=stop_reason, finished=time.ctime(), elapsed_s=time.time() - t0,
                 best_non_success=[dict(T2=t2, rate=rate, id=rid, base=b)
                                   for t2, rate, rid, b, _, _ in best_global])
    (out / f"{args.tag}_state.json").write_text(json.dumps(state, indent=1))
    fh.close()
    bh.close()
    log("done:", stop_reason, f"bases {n_bases}, evaluated {nid}, successes {n_succ}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Exact low-fault-count verification of a custom double-check circuit.

Reuses cliffordea end to end; nothing of the acceptance algorithm is
reimplemented:
  * The two circuits are written to a temporary directory laid out like
    cliffordea's bundled ``stim_files/<name>/{inner,full}.stim`` and loaded by
    cliffordea's own ``LogicalMeasurement.__init__`` (via a subclass that only
    changes ``_CIRCUIT_PARENT``). So DATA_INDICES, STABILIZER_GENERATORS and
    LOGICAL_S come from ``find_data_indices`` / ``find_stabilizer_generators`` /
    ``find_logical_s_gate`` exactly as for the bundled circuits.
  * Then the README "Complete enumeration workflow": ``uniformly_depolarize``,
    ``CliffordLogicalAnalyzer``, ``FaultCombinator.get_kept_effects``,
    ``summarize_contributions``, ``error_rates_per_kept_shot``.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
import time

import stim

from cliffordea import accept, enum
from cliffordea.enum.circuits.main import LogicalMeasurement

STATES = ("T", "S")


def _as_circuit(c) -> stim.Circuit:
    return c if isinstance(c, stim.Circuit) else stim.Circuit.from_file(str(c))


def load_measurement(stim_circuit_full, stim_circuit_inner) -> LogicalMeasurement:
    """Build a cliffordea LogicalMeasurement from in-memory circuits or paths."""
    full, inner = _as_circuit(stim_circuit_full), _as_circuit(stim_circuit_inner)
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="nnflags_") as tmp:
        # LogicalMeasurement reads <_CIRCUIT_PARENT>/d{distance}a{ancilla_count}/;
        # the numbers are only a directory label here.
        (Path(tmp) / "d0a0").mkdir()
        (Path(tmp) / "d0a0" / "inner.stim").write_text(str(inner))
        (Path(tmp) / "d0a0" / "full.stim").write_text(str(full))

        class _Custom(LogicalMeasurement):
            _CIRCUIT_PARENT = Path(tmp)

        return _Custom(distance=0, ancilla_count=0, flag_count=0)


def verify(
        stim_circuit_full,
        stim_circuit_inner,
        max_fault_count: int = 2,
        noise_level: float = 1e-3,
        states: tuple[str, ...] = STATES,
) -> dict:
    """Enumerate kept fault configurations of a double check.

    :return: {"T": {k: {"benign": n, "malignant": n}}, "S": {...},
        "summary": summarize_contributions DataFrame,
        "error_rate_per_kept_shot": {state: rate at noise_level},
        "malignant_configurations": {state: [(k, fault indices), ...]},
        "fault_count", "signature_count", "runtime_s", "settings"}.
    Malignant/benign counts are the ``configuration_count`` columns of
    cliffordea's ``summarize_contributions``.
    """
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    m = load_measurement(stim_circuit_full, stim_circuit_inner)
    noisy_circuit = enum.noise.uniformly_depolarize(m.INNER_CIRCUIT, noise_level=noise_level)
    analyzer = accept.CliffordLogicalAnalyzer(
        data_indices=m.DATA_INDICES,
        stabilizer_generators=m.STABILIZER_GENERATORS,
        logical_s=m.LOGICAL_S,
    )
    combinator = enum.FaultCombinator(noisy_circuit)
    kept = combinator.get_kept_effects(
        logical_analyzer=analyzer,
        max_fault_count=max_fault_count,
        cultivated_states=states,
    )
    summary = combinator.summarize_contributions(kept)
    result: dict = {}
    for state in states:
        result[state] = {
            k: {"benign": int(summary.loc[(state, k), ("configuration_count", "benign")]),
                "malignant": int(summary.loc[(state, k), ("configuration_count", "malignant")])}
            for k in range(max_fault_count + 1)
        }
    result["summary"] = summary
    result["error_rate_per_kept_shot"] = {
        s: float(combinator.error_rates_per_kept_shot(kept[s], noise_levels=[noise_level])[0])
        for s in states}
    result["malignant_configurations"] = {
        s: [(k, cfg) for k, effects in enumerate(kept[s])
            for p, fid, cfgs in effects.values() if p > 0 and fid != 1 for cfg in cfgs]
        for s in states}
    result["fault_count"] = combinator.fault_count
    result["signature_count"] = combinator.signature_count
    result["data_indices"] = m.DATA_INDICES
    result["runtime_s"] = time.perf_counter() - t0
    result["settings"] = dict(max_fault_count=max_fault_count, noise_level=noise_level,
                              noise_model="enum.noise.uniformly_depolarize", states=states)
    return result


def bundled_paths(name: str) -> tuple[Path, Path]:
    """(full, inner) paths of a bundled double check, e.g. "d3a6f2"."""
    d = LogicalMeasurement.__init__.__globals__["_STIM_FILES_DIR"] / "double_checks" / name
    return d / "full.stim", d / "inner.stim"
"""The 105-qubit Willow grid as a set of (row, col).

SOURCE: Google's published device specification shipped with Cirq,
``cirq_google/devices/specifications/willow_pink_d7v1-2024_08_16_device_spec_for_grid_device.proto.txt``
from the ``cirq-google==1.7.0`` wheel (copy kept in ``nnflags/data/``,
sha256 a9013ac5f78e5514d1c7349c077eee49264aa80ccd2b8b3b49190898297cee5c).
Qubit ids there are "row_col". The file lists 105 valid qubits and 182
two-qubit targets, and the targets are exactly the pairs with
|r-r'| + |c-c'| == 1 (checked in tests/test_willow.py).

Cross-checked (RESULTS_step3.md, task C): the list is identical, row by row
and with the same (row, col) labels, to the "Qubit grid" on p. 2 of Google's
Willow spec sheet (Dec 9 2024), and matches the 105 qubits of Fig. 1a of
"Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold" (arXiv:2408.13687)
up to the figure's 45-degree rotation. Everything else in nnflags only needs a
set of (row, col) tuples, so another list can be swapped in via ``grid=``.

Readout line = r + c: Google's Hardware Experiment Proposal Guidance (March
2026): "Readout lines run diagonally across the chip (i.e., such that in the
diagram on page 2 of the spec sheet, row+col = const)."
"""
from pathlib import Path
import re

Qubit = tuple[int, int]

_ROWS = {
    0: range(6, 9),
    1: range(5, 9),
    2: range(4, 11),
    3: range(3, 11),
    4: range(2, 13),
    5: range(1, 13),
    6: range(0, 15),
    7: range(2, 14),
    8: range(2, 13),
    9: range(4, 12),
    10: range(4, 11),
    11: range(6, 10),
    12: range(6, 9),
}

WILLOW: frozenset[Qubit] = frozenset((r, c) for r, cols in _ROWS.items() for c in cols)
"""The 105 Willow qubits as (row, col)."""

SPEC_FILE = Path(__file__).with_name("data") / \
    "willow_pink_d7v1-2024_08_16_device_spec_for_grid_device.proto.txt"


def neighbours(q: Qubit, grid: frozenset[Qubit] = WILLOW) -> list[Qubit]:
    """Qubits of ``grid`` at Manhattan distance 1 from ``q``."""
    r, c = q
    return [n for n in ((r - 1, c), (r + 1, c), (r, c - 1), (r, c + 1)) if n in grid]


def is_unit_step(a, b) -> bool:
    """Axis-aligned distance 1. Equals |r-r'|+|c-c'| == 1 on integer points,
    and also rejects half-integer diagonal steps such as (1,1)-(1.5,0.5)."""
    return sorted((abs(a[0] - b[0]), abs(a[1] - b[1]))) == [0, 1]


def is_edge(a: Qubit, b: Qubit, grid: frozenset[Qubit] | None = WILLOW) -> bool:
    """Whether (a, b) is an edge of the hardware graph G (grid=None: any points)."""
    return (grid is None or (a in grid and b in grid)) and is_unit_step(a, b)


def edges(grid: frozenset[Qubit] = WILLOW) -> set[tuple[Qubit, Qubit]]:
    """All edges of G as sorted pairs."""
    return {tuple(sorted((q, n))) for q in grid for n in neighbours(q, grid)}


def readout_line(q: Qubit) -> int:
    """Readout line of (r, c) = r + c (first-ex.md; Google's proposal guidance)."""
    return q[0] + q[1]


def load_spec_file(path: Path = SPEC_FILE) -> tuple[set[Qubit], set[tuple[Qubit, Qubit]]]:
    """Parse qubits and two-qubit targets from the Cirq device-spec text proto."""
    text = path.read_text()
    to_q = lambda s: tuple(map(int, s.split("_")))
    qubits = {to_q(s) for s in re.findall(r'valid_qubits: "(\d+_\d+)"', text)}
    pairs = re.findall(r'ids: "(\d+_\d+)"\s*ids: "(\d+_\d+)"', text)
    return qubits, {tuple(sorted((to_q(a), to_q(b)))) for a, b in pairs}


def ascii_map(grid: frozenset[Qubit] = WILLOW, marks: dict[Qubit, str] | None = None) -> str:
    """Text picture of the grid; ``marks`` overrides the '#' for given qubits."""
    marks = marks or {}
    rows = range(min(r for r, _ in grid), max(r for r, _ in grid) + 1)
    cols = range(min(c for _, c in grid), max(c for _, c in grid) + 1)
    return "\n".join(
        f"{r:2d} " + "".join(marks.get((r, c), "#") if (r, c) in grid else "." for c in cols)
        for r in rows)

"""Exact low-fault-count verification of a custom double-check circuit.

Reuses cliffordea end to end; nothing of the acceptance algorithm is
reimplemented:
  * The two circuits are written to a temporary directory laid out like
    cliffordea's bundled ``stim_files/<name>/{inner,full}.stim`` and loaded by
    cliffordea's own ``LogicalMeasurement.__init__`` (via a subclass that only
    changes ``_CIRCUIT_PARENT``). So DATA_INDICES, STABILIZER_GENERATORS and
    LOGICAL_S come from ``find_data_indices`` / ``find_stabilizer_generators`` /
    ``find_logical_s_gate`` exactly as for the bundled circuits.
  * Then the README "Complete enumeration workflow": ``uniformly_depolarize``,
    ``CliffordLogicalAnalyzer``, ``FaultCombinator.get_kept_effects``,
    ``summarize_contributions``, ``error_rates_per_kept_shot``.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
import time

import stim

from cliffordea import accept, enum
from cliffordea.enum.circuits.main import LogicalMeasurement

STATES = ("T", "S")


def _as_circuit(c) -> stim.Circuit:
    return c if isinstance(c, stim.Circuit) else stim.Circuit.from_file(str(c))


def load_measurement(stim_circuit_full, stim_circuit_inner) -> LogicalMeasurement:
    """Build a cliffordea LogicalMeasurement from in-memory circuits or paths."""
    full, inner = _as_circuit(stim_circuit_full), _as_circuit(stim_circuit_inner)
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="nnflags_") as tmp:
        # LogicalMeasurement reads <_CIRCUIT_PARENT>/d{distance}a{ancilla_count}/;
        # the numbers are only a directory label here.
        (Path(tmp) / "d0a0").mkdir()
        (Path(tmp) / "d0a0" / "inner.stim").write_text(str(inner))
        (Path(tmp) / "d0a0" / "full.stim").write_text(str(full))

        class _Custom(LogicalMeasurement):
            _CIRCUIT_PARENT = Path(tmp)

        return _Custom(distance=0, ancilla_count=0, flag_count=0)


def verify(
        stim_circuit_full,
        stim_circuit_inner,
        max_fault_count: int = 2,
        noise_level: float = 1e-3,
        states: tuple[str, ...] = STATES,
) -> dict:
    """Enumerate kept fault configurations of a double check.

    :return: {"T": {k: {"benign": n, "malignant": n}}, "S": {...},
        "summary": summarize_contributions DataFrame,
        "error_rate_per_kept_shot": {state: rate at noise_level},
        "malignant_configurations": {state: [(k, fault indices), ...]},
        "fault_count", "signature_count", "runtime_s", "settings"}.
    Malignant/benign counts are the ``configuration_count`` columns of
    cliffordea's ``summarize_contributions``.
    """
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    m = load_measurement(stim_circuit_full, stim_circuit_inner)
    noisy_circuit = enum.noise.uniformly_depolarize(m.INNER_CIRCUIT, noise_level=noise_level)
    analyzer = accept.CliffordLogicalAnalyzer(
        data_indices=m.DATA_INDICES,
        stabilizer_generators=m.STABILIZER_GENERATORS,
        logical_s=m.LOGICAL_S,
    )
    combinator = enum.FaultCombinator(noisy_circuit)
    kept = combinator.get_kept_effects(
        logical_analyzer=analyzer,
        max_fault_count=max_fault_count,
        cultivated_states=states,
    )
    summary = combinator.summarize_contributions(kept)
    result: dict = {}
    for state in states:
        result[state] = {
            k: {"benign": int(summary.loc[(state, k), ("configuration_count", "benign")]),
                "malignant": int(summary.loc[(state, k), ("configuration_count", "malignant")])}
            for k in range(max_fault_count + 1)
        }
    result["summary"] = summary
    result["error_rate_per_kept_shot"] = {
        s: float(combinator.error_rates_per_kept_shot(kept[s], noise_levels=[noise_level])[0])
        for s in states}
    result["malignant_configurations"] = {
        s: [(k, cfg) for k, effects in enumerate(kept[s])
            for p, fid, cfgs in effects.values() if p > 0 and fid != 1 for cfg in cfgs]
        for s in states}
    result["fault_count"] = combinator.fault_count
    result["signature_count"] = combinator.signature_count
    result["data_indices"] = m.DATA_INDICES
    result["runtime_s"] = time.perf_counter() - t0
    result["settings"] = dict(max_fault_count=max_fault_count, noise_level=noise_level,
                              noise_model="enum.noise.uniformly_depolarize", states=states)
    return result


def bundled_paths(name: str) -> tuple[Path, Path]:
    """(full, inner) paths of a bundled double check, e.g. "d3a6f2"."""
    d = LogicalMeasurement.__init__.__globals__["_STIM_FILES_DIR"] / "double_checks" / name
    return d / "full.stim", d / "inner.stim"
"""The 105-qubit Willow grid as a set of (row, col).

SOURCE: Google's published device specification shipped with Cirq,
``cirq_google/devices/specifications/willow_pink_d7v1-2024_08_16_device_spec_for_grid_device.proto.txt``
from the ``cirq-google==1.7.0`` wheel (copy kept in ``nnflags/data/``,
sha256 a9013ac5f78e5514d1c7349c077eee49264aa80ccd2b8b3b49190898297cee5c).
Qubit ids there are "row_col". The file lists 105 valid qubits and 182
two-qubit targets, and the targets are exactly the pairs with
|r-r'| + |c-c'| == 1 (checked in tests/test_willow.py).

Cross-checked (RESULTS_step3.md, task C): the list is identical, row by row
and with the same (row, col) labels, to the "Qubit grid" on p. 2 of Google's
Willow spec sheet (Dec 9 2024), and matches the 105 qubits of Fig. 1a of
"Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold" (arXiv:2408.13687)
up to the figure's 45-degree rotation. Everything else in nnflags only needs a
set of (row, col) tuples, so another list can be swapped in via ``grid=``.

Readout line = r + c: Google's Hardware Experiment Proposal Guidance (March
2026): "Readout lines run diagonally across the chip (i.e., such that in the
diagram on page 2 of the spec sheet, row+col = const)."
"""
from pathlib import Path
import re

Qubit = tuple[int, int]

_ROWS = {
    0: range(6, 9),
    1: range(5, 9),
    2: range(4, 11),
    3: range(3, 11),
    4: range(2, 13),
    5: range(1, 13),
    6: range(0, 15),
    7: range(2, 14),
    8: range(2, 13),
    9: range(4, 12),
    10: range(4, 11),
    11: range(6, 10),
    12: range(6, 9),
}

WILLOW: frozenset[Qubit] = frozenset((r, c) for r, cols in _ROWS.items() for c in cols)
"""The 105 Willow qubits as (row, col)."""

SPEC_FILE = Path(__file__).with_name("data") / \
    "willow_pink_d7v1-2024_08_16_device_spec_for_grid_device.proto.txt"


def neighbours(q: Qubit, grid: frozenset[Qubit] = WILLOW) -> list[Qubit]:
    """Qubits of ``grid`` at Manhattan distance 1 from ``q``."""
    r, c = q
    return [n for n in ((r - 1, c), (r + 1, c), (r, c - 1), (r, c + 1)) if n in grid]


def is_unit_step(a, b) -> bool:
    """Axis-aligned distance 1. Equals |r-r'|+|c-c'| == 1 on integer points,
    and also rejects half-integer diagonal steps such as (1,1)-(1.5,0.5)."""
    return sorted((abs(a[0] - b[0]), abs(a[1] - b[1]))) == [0, 1]


def is_edge(a: Qubit, b: Qubit, grid: frozenset[Qubit] | None = WILLOW) -> bool:
    """Whether (a, b) is an edge of the hardware graph G (grid=None: any points)."""
    return (grid is None or (a in grid and b in grid)) and is_unit_step(a, b)


def edges(grid: frozenset[Qubit] = WILLOW) -> set[tuple[Qubit, Qubit]]:
    """All edges of G as sorted pairs."""
    return {tuple(sorted((q, n))) for q in grid for n in neighbours(q, grid)}


def readout_line(q: Qubit) -> int:
    """Readout line of (r, c) = r + c (first-ex.md; Google's proposal guidance)."""
    return q[0] + q[1]


def load_spec_file(path: Path = SPEC_FILE) -> tuple[set[Qubit], set[tuple[Qubit, Qubit]]]:
    """Parse qubits and two-qubit targets from the Cirq device-spec text proto."""
    text = path.read_text()
    to_q = lambda s: tuple(map(int, s.split("_")))
    qubits = {to_q(s) for s in re.findall(r'valid_qubits: "(\d+_\d+)"', text)}
    pairs = re.findall(r'ids: "(\d+_\d+)"\s*ids: "(\d+_\d+)"', text)
    return qubits, {tuple(sorted((to_q(a), to_q(b)))) for a, b in pairs}


def ascii_map(grid: frozenset[Qubit] = WILLOW, marks: dict[Qubit, str] | None = None) -> str:
    """Text picture of the grid; ``marks`` overrides the '#' for given qubits."""
    marks = marks or {}
    rows = range(min(r for r, _ in grid), max(r for r, _ in grid) + 1)
    cols = range(min(c for _, c in grid), max(c for _, c in grid) + 1)
    return "\n".join(
        f"{r:2d} " + "".join(marks.get((r, c), "#") if (r, c) in grid else "." for c in cols)
        for r in rows)

"""Option-1 task C: "same code + same double check" equivalence checker.

``check_equivalence(inner)`` verifies, for a candidate cliffordea inner circuit
(MPP marker on the data, double check, trailing reset), with cliffordea's own
derivations (``verify.load_measurement`` -> ``find_data_indices``,
``find_stabilizer_generators``, ``find_logical_s_gate``) and stim:

  (i)   code: the data code is the d=3 colour code of d3a6 up to a relabelling
        of the data qubits (stabiliser supports AND the logical-S sublattice
        map onto d3a6's), and the full circuit's MPP framing is consistent.
  (ii)  check: the circuit (MPP marker removed) acts on the data as a
        projective measurement of X_L = X^(x)7 -- cliffordea's H_XY check in
        the inner frame (enum/circuits/main.py:42-45):
          * forward check: the detector containing the MPP record compares
            the MPP with records R1, and stim flow  X_L -> rec[R1]  holds;
          * time-reversed check: a detector without the MPP record contains
            records of R1 plus records R2 measured later, and  X_L -> rec[R2]
            holds (the unfold re-reads the same logical after the reset);
          * X_L and every generator of its commutant (X_q, Z_a Z_b) pass
            unchanged:  P -> P xor rec[...] ;  Z_L has no such flow.
  (iii) reverse: in canonical CX form (``absorb_hadamards``), the two-qubit
        gate layers of the unfold are exactly the fold's layers in reverse
        order, and U_unfold * U_fold = identity (stim tableaux). Gates on
        ``flag_qubits`` are excluded (flags are added gates, decision 4).
  (iv)  all detectors are deterministic (stim, noiseless circuit).

Fold / unfold: the TICKs strictly between the ancilla preparation layer and
the forward-check measurement TICK, and between that TICK and the final
measurement TICK (re-preparations of the measured qubits are absorbed by the
canonical form).
"""
import itertools
from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import stim

from cliffordea.enum.circuit_tools import split_by_ticks

from nnflags.verify import bundled_paths, load_measurement

_ANNOT = ("DETECTOR", "OBSERVABLE_INCLUDE")
_SKIP = ("QUBIT_COORDS", "SHIFT_COORDS")


# ---- layered representation with global measurement ids -----------------------

@dataclass
class Op:
    name: str
    targets: list          # qubit ints (MPP: stim targets)
    args: list = field(default_factory=list)
    ids: list = field(default_factory=list)   # global measurement ids
    tag: str = ""


def to_layers(circuit: stim.Circuit):
    """[[Op | ('det', name, args, ids) | ('coords', instr)]], one list per TICK,
    with every measurement split per target and given a global id."""
    layers, n = [], 0
def is_deterministic(circuit: stim.Circuit) -> bool:
    try:
        circuit.detector_error_model(allow_gauge_detectors=False)
        return True
    except ValueError:
        return False


def _strip_mpp(circuit):
    """Inner circuit without its MPP marker (detectors referring to the MPP
    record lose that record) and the MPP's global measurement ids."""
    layers = to_layers(circuit)
    mpp_ids = set()
    for items in layers:
        for it in list(items):
            if isinstance(it, Op) and it.name == "MPP":
                mpp_ids.update(it.ids)
                items.remove(it)
    for items in layers:
        for k, it in enumerate(items):
            if not isinstance(it, Op) and it[0] == "det":
                items[k] = (it[0], it[1], it[2], [g for g in it[3] if g not in mpp_ids],
                            [g for g in it[3] if g in mpp_ids])
    return layers, mpp_ids


def _detectors(layers):
    """Global ids of each DETECTOR (MPP ids kept, also after ``_strip_mpp``)."""
    return [it[3] + (it[4] if len(it) > 4 else []) for items in layers for it in items
            if not isinstance(it, Op) and it[0] == "det" and it[1] == "DETECTOR"]


def _meas_order(layers):
    """Global measurement ids in record order (MPP excluded) -> record index."""
    ids = [g for items in layers for it in items if isinstance(it, Op) for g in it.ids]
    return {g: i for i, g in enumerate(ids)}


def _flow(circuit, n_records, inp, out, recs):
    terms = " xor ".join(f"rec[{r - n_records}]" for r in sorted(recs))
    text = f"{inp} -> {out}" + (f" xor {terms}" if terms else "")
    return circuit.has_flow(stim.Flow(text)), text


def _pauli(nq, qubits, p):
    s = ["_"] * nq
    for q in qubits:
        s[q] = p
    return "".join(s)


def check_logical_action(inner: stim.Circuit, data):
    """Check (ii). Returns dict with the flows found."""
    layers, mpp_ids = _strip_mpp(inner)
    bare = from_layers(layers)
    nq = inner.num_qubits
    order = _meas_order(layers)
    nrec = len(order)
    xl = _pauli(nq, data, "X")
    dets = _detectors(layers)
    fwd = [d for d in dets if set(d) & mpp_ids]
    res = {"forward_detectors": [], "reverse_detectors": [], "commutant": {}, "ok": True}
    r1_all = set()
    for d in fwd:
        r1 = {order[g] for g in d if g not in mpp_ids}
        ok, text = _flow(bare, nrec, xl, "1", r1)
        res["forward_detectors"].append(dict(records=sorted(r1), flow=text, holds=ok))
        res["ok"] &= ok
        r1_all |= r1
    if not fwd:
        res["ok"] = False
        res["error"] = "no detector contains the MPP record"
        return res
    last_r1 = max(r1_all)
    for d in dets:
        if set(d) & mpp_ids:
            continue
        recs = {order[g] for g in d}
        r1 = recs & r1_all
        r2 = recs - r1_all
        if r1 and r2 and min(r2) > last_r1:
            ok, text = _flow(bare, nrec, xl, "1", r2)
            res["reverse_detectors"].append(dict(records=sorted(recs), r2=sorted(r2),
                                                 flow=text, holds=ok))
    res["time_reversed_check"] = any(x["holds"] for x in res["reverse_detectors"])
    res["ok"] &= res["time_reversed_check"]
    # Commutant of X_L passes unchanged; Z_L does not.
    gens = {f"X{q}": _pauli(nq, [q], "X") for q in data}
    ds = sorted(data)
    gens.update({f"Z{a}Z{b}": _pauli(nq, [a, b], "Z") for a, b in zip(ds, ds[1:])})
    gens["X_L"] = xl
    for k, p in gens.items():
        sol = bare.solve_flow_measurements([stim.Flow(f"{p} -> {p}")])[0]
        res["commutant"][k] = sol is not None
        res["ok"] &= sol is not None
    zl = _pauli(nq, data, "Z")
    res["Z_L_preserved"] = bare.solve_flow_measurements([stim.Flow(f"{zl} -> {zl}")])[0] is not None
    res["ok"] &= not res["Z_L_preserved"]
    return res


def fold_unfold(inner: stim.Circuit, data, flag_qubits=()):
    """Two-qubit layers (flags excluded) of fold and unfold in canonical CX form,
    and the forward-check TICK, for check (iii)."""
    cx, info = absorb_hadamards(inner, data)
    layers = to_layers(cx)
    _, mpp_ids = _strip_mpp(cx)
    fwd = [d for d in _detectors(layers) if set(d) & mpp_ids]
    fwd_ids = {g for d in fwd for g in d if g not in mpp_ids}
    tick_of = {g: t for t, items in enumerate(layers) for it in items if isinstance(it, Op)
               for g in it.ids}
    t_check = max(tick_of[g] for g in fwd_ids)
    meas_ticks = sorted({tick_of[g] for g in tick_of if g not in mpp_ids})
    t_final = meas_ticks[-1]
    flags = set(flag_qubits)

    def two_q(t0, t1):
        out = []
        for t in range(t0, t1):
            gates = sorted((it.name, *it.targets) for it in layers[t] if isinstance(it, Op)
                           and stim.gate_data(it.name).is_two_qubit_gate
                           and not (set(it.targets) & flags))
            if gates:
                out.append(tuple(gates))
        return out

    return two_q(0, t_check), two_q(t_check + 1, t_final), cx, info


def _tableau(nq, layers_):
    c = stim.Circuit(f"I {nq - 1}")
    for gates in layers_:
        for name, a, b in gates:
            c.append(name, [a, b])
    return stim.Tableau.from_circuit(c)


def check_equivalence(inner, full=None, flag_qubits=(), reference="d3a6") -> dict:
    """Run checks (i)-(iv) on ``inner`` with ``full`` = the full circuit given
    to verify() (cliffordea reads only its MPPs and S layers; default: the
    bundled reference full circuit). ``flag_qubits`` are excluded from (iii).
    :return: {"i_code", "ii_check", "iii_reverse", "iv_deterministic": {"ok", ...}, "ok"}."""
    inner = inner if isinstance(inner, stim.Circuit) else stim.Circuit.from_file(str(inner))
    ref_full, ref_inner = bundled_paths(reference)
    if full is None:
        full = ref_full
    out = {}
    meas = load_measurement(full, inner)
    ref = load_measurement(ref_full, ref_inner)
    data = meas.DATA_INDICES
    perm = _data_perm_to_reference(meas, ref)
    out["i_code"] = dict(ok=perm is not None, data=data, relabelling=perm,
                         stabilizers=sorted(map(sorted, meas._STABILIZER_GENERATOR_INDICES)),
                         logical_s=str(meas.LOGICAL_S).split("\n"))
    out["ii_check"] = check_logical_action(inner, data)
    try:
        fold, unfold, cx, info = fold_unfold(inner, data, flag_qubits)
    except ValueError as e:  # e.g. no forward-check detector to split fold / unfold
        out["iii_reverse"] = dict(ok=False, error=str(e))
    else:
        exact = unfold == fold[::-1]
        nq = inner.num_qubits
        identity = (_tableau(nq, fold + unfold) == stim.Tableau(nq))
        out["iii_reverse"] = dict(ok=exact and identity and len(fold) > 0,
                                  exact_layer_reverse=exact, tableau_identity=identity,
                                  fold=fold, unfold=unfold, canonical_non_cx=info["non_cx"])
    out["iv_deterministic"] = dict(ok=is_deterministic(inner))
    out["ok"] = all(out[k]["ok"] for k in ("i_code", "ii_check", "iii_reverse", "iv_deterministic"))
    return out

"""Option-1 task C: "same code + same double check" equivalence checker.

``check_equivalence(inner)`` verifies, for a candidate cliffordea inner circuit
(MPP marker on the data, double check, trailing reset), with cliffordea's own
derivations (``verify.load_measurement`` -> ``find_data_indices``,
``find_stabilizer_generators``, ``find_logical_s_gate``) and stim:

  (i)   code: the data code is the d=3 colour code of d3a6 up to a relabelling
        of the data qubits (stabiliser supports AND the logical-S sublattice
        map onto d3a6's), and the full circuit's MPP framing is consistent.
  (ii)  check: the circuit (MPP marker removed) acts on the data as a
        projective measurement of X_L = X^(x)7 -- cliffordea's H_XY check in
        the inner frame (enum/circuits/main.py:42-45):
          * forward check: the detector containing the MPP record compares
            the MPP with records R1, and stim flow  X_L -> rec[R1]  holds;
          * time-reversed check: a detector without the MPP record contains
            records of R1 plus records R2 measured later, and  X_L -> rec[R2]
            holds (the unfold re-reads the same logical after the reset);
          * X_L and every generator of its commutant (X_q, Z_a Z_b) pass
            unchanged:  P -> P xor rec[...] ;  Z_L has no such flow.
  (iii) reverse: in canonical CX form (``absorb_hadamards``), the two-qubit
        gate layers of the unfold are exactly the fold's layers in reverse
        order, and U_unfold * U_fold = identity (stim tableaux). Gates on
        ``flag_qubits`` are excluded (flags are added gates, decision 4).
  (iv)  all detectors are deterministic (stim, noiseless circuit).

Fold / unfold: the TICKs strictly between the ancilla preparation layer and
the forward-check measurement TICK, and between that TICK and the final
measurement TICK (re-preparations of the measured qubits are absorbed by the
canonical form).
"""
import itertools
from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import stim

from cliffordea.enum.circuit_tools import split_by_ticks

from nnflags.verify import bundled_paths, load_measurement

_ANNOT = ("DETECTOR", "OBSERVABLE_INCLUDE")
_SKIP = ("QUBIT_COORDS", "SHIFT_COORDS")


# ---- layered representation with global measurement ids -----------------------

@dataclass
class Op:
    name: str
    targets: list          # qubit ints (MPP: stim targets)
    args: list = field(default_factory=list)
    ids: list = field(default_factory=list)   # global measurement ids
    tag: str = ""


def to_layers(circuit: stim.Circuit):
    """[[Op | ('det', name, args, ids) | ('coords', instr)]], one list per TICK,
    with every measurement split per target and given a global id."""
    layers, n = [], 0
def is_deterministic(circuit: stim.Circuit) -> bool:
    try:
        circuit.detector_error_model(allow_gauge_detectors=False)
        return True
    except ValueError:
        return False


def _strip_mpp(circuit):
    """Inner circuit without its MPP marker (detectors referring to the MPP
    record lose that record) and the MPP's global measurement ids."""
    layers = to_layers(circuit)
    mpp_ids = set()
    for items in layers:
        for it in list(items):
            if isinstance(it, Op) and it.name == "MPP":
                mpp_ids.update(it.ids)
                items.remove(it)
    for items in layers:
        for k, it in enumerate(items):
            if not isinstance(it, Op) and it[0] == "det":
                items[k] = (it[0], it[1], it[2], [g for g in it[3] if g not in mpp_ids],
                            [g for g in it[3] if g in mpp_ids])
    return layers, mpp_ids


def _detectors(layers):
    """Global ids of each DETECTOR (MPP ids kept, also after ``_strip_mpp``)."""
    return [it[3] + (it[4] if len(it) > 4 else []) for items in layers for it in items
            if not isinstance(it, Op) and it[0] == "det" and it[1] == "DETECTOR"]


def _meas_order(layers):
    """Global measurement ids in record order (MPP excluded) -> record index."""
    ids = [g for items in layers for it in items if isinstance(it, Op) for g in it.ids]
    return {g: i for i, g in enumerate(ids)}


def _flow(circuit, n_records, inp, out, recs):
    terms = " xor ".join(f"rec[{r - n_records}]" for r in sorted(recs))
    text = f"{inp} -> {out}" + (f" xor {terms}" if terms else "")
    return circuit.has_flow(stim.Flow(text)), text


def _pauli(nq, qubits, p):
    s = ["_"] * nq
    for q in qubits:
        s[q] = p
    return "".join(s)


def check_logical_action(inner: stim.Circuit, data):
    """Check (ii). Returns dict with the flows found."""
    layers, mpp_ids = _strip_mpp(inner)
    bare = from_layers(layers)
    nq = inner.num_qubits
    order = _meas_order(layers)
    nrec = len(order)
    xl = _pauli(nq, data, "X")
    dets = _detectors(layers)
    fwd = [d for d in dets if set(d) & mpp_ids]
    res = {"forward_detectors": [], "reverse_detectors": [], "commutant": {}, "ok": True}
    r1_all = set()
    for d in fwd:
        r1 = {order[g] for g in d if g not in mpp_ids}
        ok, text = _flow(bare, nrec, xl, "1", r1)
        res["forward_detectors"].append(dict(records=sorted(r1), flow=text, holds=ok))
        res["ok"] &= ok
        r1_all |= r1
    if not fwd:
        res["ok"] = False
        res["error"] = "no detector contains the MPP record"
        return res
    last_r1 = max(r1_all)
    for d in dets:
        if set(d) & mpp_ids:
            continue
        recs = {order[g] for g in d}
        r1 = recs & r1_all
        r2 = recs - r1_all
        if r1 and r2 and min(r2) > last_r1:
            ok, text = _flow(bare, nrec, xl, "1", r2)
            res["reverse_detectors"].append(dict(records=sorted(recs), r2=sorted(r2),
                                                 flow=text, holds=ok))
    res["time_reversed_check"] = any(x["holds"] for x in res["reverse_detectors"])
    res["ok"] &= res["time_reversed_check"]
    # Commutant of X_L passes unchanged; Z_L does not.
    gens = {f"X{q}": _pauli(nq, [q], "X") for q in data}
    ds = sorted(data)
    gens.update({f"Z{a}Z{b}": _pauli(nq, [a, b], "Z") for a, b in zip(ds, ds[1:])})
    gens["X_L"] = xl
    for k, p in gens.items():
        sol = bare.solve_flow_measurements([stim.Flow(f"{p} -> {p}")])[0]
        res["commutant"][k] = sol is not None
        res["ok"] &= sol is not None
    zl = _pauli(nq, data, "Z")
    res["Z_L_preserved"] = bare.solve_flow_measurements([stim.Flow(f"{zl} -> {zl}")])[0] is not None
    res["ok"] &= not res["Z_L_preserved"]
    return res


def fold_unfold(inner: stim.Circuit, data, flag_qubits=()):
    """Two-qubit layers (flags excluded) of fold and unfold in canonical CX form,
    and the forward-check TICK, for check (iii)."""
    cx, info = absorb_hadamards(inner, data)
    layers = to_layers(cx)
    _, mpp_ids = _strip_mpp(cx)
    fwd = [d for d in _detectors(layers) if set(d) & mpp_ids]
    fwd_ids = {g for d in fwd for g in d if g not in mpp_ids}
    tick_of = {g: t for t, items in enumerate(layers) for it in items if isinstance(it, Op)
               for g in it.ids}
    t_check = max(tick_of[g] for g in fwd_ids)
    meas_ticks = sorted({tick_of[g] for g in tick_of if g not in mpp_ids})
    t_final = meas_ticks[-1]
    flags = set(flag_qubits)

    def two_q(t0, t1):
        out = []
        for t in range(t0, t1):
            gates = sorted((it.name, *it.targets) for it in layers[t] if isinstance(it, Op)
                           and stim.gate_data(it.name).is_two_qubit_gate
                           and not (set(it.targets) & flags))
            if gates:
                out.append(tuple(gates))
        return out

    return two_q(0, t_check), two_q(t_check + 1, t_final), cx, info


def _tableau(nq, layers_):
    c = stim.Circuit(f"I {nq - 1}")
    for gates in layers_:
        for name, a, b in gates:
            c.append(name, [a, b])
    return stim.Tableau.from_circuit(c)


def check_equivalence(inner, full=None, flag_qubits=(), reference="d3a6") -> dict:
    """Run checks (i)-(iv) on ``inner`` with ``full`` = the full circuit given
    to verify() (cliffordea reads only its MPPs and S layers; default: the
    bundled reference full circuit). ``flag_qubits`` are excluded from (iii).
    :return: {"i_code", "ii_check", "iii_reverse", "iv_deterministic": {"ok", ...}, "ok"}."""
    inner = inner if isinstance(inner, stim.Circuit) else stim.Circuit.from_file(str(inner))
    ref_full, ref_inner = bundled_paths(reference)
    if full is None:
        full = ref_full
    out = {}
    meas = load_measurement(full, inner)
    ref = load_measurement(ref_full, ref_inner)
    data = meas.DATA_INDICES
    perm = _data_perm_to_reference(meas, ref)
    out["i_code"] = dict(ok=perm is not None, data=data, relabelling=perm,
                         stabilizers=sorted(map(sorted, meas._STABILIZER_GENERATOR_INDICES)),
                         logical_s=str(meas.LOGICAL_S).split("\n"))
    out["ii_check"] = check_logical_action(inner, data)
    try:
        fold, unfold, cx, info = fold_unfold(inner, data, flag_qubits)
    except ValueError as e:  # e.g. no forward-check detector to split fold / unfold
        out["iii_reverse"] = dict(ok=False, error=str(e))
    else:
        exact = unfold == fold[::-1]
        nq = inner.num_qubits
        identity = (_tableau(nq, fold + unfold) == stim.Tableau(nq))
        out["iii_reverse"] = dict(ok=exact and identity and len(fold) > 0,
                                  exact_layer_reverse=exact, tableau_identity=identity,
                                  fold=fold, unfold=unfold, canonical_non_cx=info["non_cx"])
    out["iv_deterministic"] = dict(ok=is_deterministic(inner))
    out["ok"] = all(out[k]["ok"] for k in ("i_code", "ii_check", "iii_reverse", "iv_deterministic"))
    return out

"""Option-1 task B: fault distance of Google's as-run double check (G4).

G4 = rosenfeld2512_G4.stim, the complete Fig. 2 cultivation circuit of
Rosenfeld et al., arXiv:2512.13908, at Willow coordinates (CZ + H gate set,
Z-basis measurement, no MPP; non-Clifford gates appear as tagged identities).

TICK map of G4 (0-based, ``split_by_ticks``):
   0-3    injection on qubit 5 (H_YZ[conjugate] S[injection] H_YZ[conjugate])
   4-25   encoding into the d=3 colour code; TICK 25: M 4 1 6 9 (checks)
   26     R 4 1 9 6
   27-30  transversal T on data 3 0 8 5 11 2 10: I[conjugate] I[echo]
          I[T_gate] I[conjugate]
   31-39  FOLD (H / CZ layers)
   40     M 9 6 (mid-check measurement)          41  R 9 6
   42-50  UNFOLD (time reverse of 31-39, except that the H on ancillas 1, 4
          that starts the fold is applied at TICK 55 instead)
   51-54  transversal T^dagger: I[conjugate] I[echo] I[T_dagger_gate] I[conjugate]
   55     H on all qubits but 7                    56  M on all 12 qubits

Data (T-gate targets) = 0 2 3 5 8 10 11; ancillas = 1 4 6 7 9. The double
check = TICKs 31-50 plus the ancilla part of the readout (TICKs 55-56).
Rosenfeld et al. (Sec. I): T := exp(-i pi sigma_y / 8) and the measured
operator is H = T^dag X T; "[conjugate]" is the H_YZ basis change that turns
the Z rotation into this Y rotation (same tag around S[injection], TICKs 0-2).

Extraction into cliffordea's inner-circuit conventions (enum/circuits/main.py:42-54):
  * TICK 0: QUBIT_COORDS (G4's), noiseless ``MPP X^(x)7`` marker on the data.
  * TICK 1: ``R 4 1 9 6`` (G4 TICK 26) + ``R 7``: G4 never resets qubit 7 (it
    is in |0> from the start of the experiment; checked by simulation).
  * G4 TICKs 31-50 verbatim, except: identity placeholders I[...] dropped
    (cliffordea's noise model gives an I gate and an idle qubit the same
    DEPOLARIZE1(p), enum/noise/_noise.py:278-317; checked numerically), and
    ``M 9 6`` -> ``MR 9 6`` (cliffordea: a measured ancilla that is used
    again must be MR, main.py:46-50; the following ``R 9 6`` is kept, so the
    TICK structure is G4's).
  * Ancilla readout: ``H 4 1 9 6`` then ``M 4 1 9 6 7`` (G4 TICKs 55-56
    restricted to the ancillas; it commutes with the T^dagger on the data,
    so it is moved before it, as in cliffordea's own inner circuits).
  * Detectors: G4's, restricted to these measurements. The forward-check
    detector "M 9" becomes "M 9 xor MPP" (G4's stand-in state is |+_L>, so
    there it is deterministic alone; in the inner frame the reference is
    the MPP marker).
  * Trailing ``R`` of all ancillas (main.py:51-53).
  -> variant "native" (CZ + H, G4's TICKs).

  per-qubit frame, CZ -> CX, R/M -> RX/MX where framed, H-only TICKs gone,
  'M; TICK; R' merged into MR/MRX (the conversion cliffordea's d3a4 uses for
  the same experiment).

logical-S "majority" sublattice and T^dag on the rest (Z rotations,
accept/logical_analyzers.py:178-189); G4 applies T_y^dag = exp(+i pi Y/8)
uniformly. With W = H_NYZ on the majority, H_YZ on the minority (per qubit
W T_y^dag W^dag = T_z on majority, T_z^dag on minority), the G4 protocol is

check run inside cliffordea's standard T_z convention, like d3a6/d3a4).

   27-30  transversal T on data 3 0 8 5 11 2 10: I[conjugate] I[echo]
          I[T_gate] I[conjugate]
   31-39  FOLD (H / CZ layers)
   40     M 9 6 (mid-check measurement)          41  R 9 6
   42-50  UNFOLD (time reverse of 31-39, except that the H on ancillas 1, 4
          that starts the fold is applied at TICK 55 instead)
   51-54  transversal T^dagger: I[conjugate] I[echo] I[T_dagger_gate] I[conjugate]
   55     H on all qubits but 7                    56  M on all 12 qubits

Data (T-gate targets) = 0 2 3 5 8 10 11; ancillas = 1 4 6 7 9. The double
check = TICKs 31-50 plus the ancilla part of the readout (TICKs 55-56).
Rosenfeld et al. (Sec. I): T := exp(-i pi sigma_y / 8) and the measured
operator is H = T^dag X T; "[conjugate]" is the H_YZ basis change that turns
the Z rotation into this Y rotation (same tag around S[injection], TICKs 0-2).

Extraction into cliffordea's inner-circuit conventions (enum/circuits/main.py:42-54):
  * TICK 0: QUBIT_COORDS (G4's), noiseless ``MPP X^(x)7`` marker on the data.
  * TICK 1: ``R 4 1 9 6`` (G4 TICK 26) + ``R 7``: G4 never resets qubit 7 (it
    is in |0> from the start of the experiment; checked by simulation).
  * G4 TICKs 31-50 verbatim, except: identity placeholders I[...] dropped
    (cliffordea's noise model gives an I gate and an idle qubit the same
    DEPOLARIZE1(p), enum/noise/_noise.py:278-317; checked numerically), and
    ``M 9 6`` -> ``MR 9 6`` (cliffordea: a measured ancilla that is used
    again must be MR, main.py:46-50; the following ``R 9 6`` is kept, so the
    TICK structure is G4's).
  * Ancilla readout: ``H 4 1 9 6`` then ``M 4 1 9 6 7`` (G4 TICKs 55-56
    restricted to the ancillas; it commutes with the T^dagger on the data,
    so it is moved before it, as in cliffordea's own inner circuits).
  * Detectors: G4's, restricted to these measurements. The forward-check
    detector "M 9" becomes "M 9 xor MPP" (G4's stand-in state is |+_L>, so
    there it is deterministic alone; in the inner frame the reference is
    the MPP marker).
  * Trailing ``R`` of all ancillas (main.py:51-53).
  -> variant "native" (CZ + H, G4's TICKs).
  "cx" = ``equivalence.absorb_hadamards(native)``: every H pushed into a
  per-qubit frame, CZ -> CX, R/M -> RX/MX where framed, H-only TICKs gone,
  'M; TICK; R' merged into MR/MRX (the conversion cliffordea's d3a4 uses for
  the same experiment).

T-gate convention. cliffordea pushes the data effect through T on the
logical-S "majority" sublattice and T^dag on the rest (Z rotations,
accept/logical_analyzers.py:178-189); G4 applies T_y^dag = exp(+i pi Y/8)
uniformly. With W = H_NYZ on the majority, H_YZ on the minority (per qubit
W T_y^dag W^dag = T_z on majority, T_z^dag on minority), the G4 protocol is
cliffordea's protocol for the inner circuit W^dag . DC . W. frame="as_run"
inserts W^dag after the MPP marker (TICK 0) and W in the trailing reset TICK;
both TICKs are noiseless in uniformly_depolarize (enum/noise/main.py:39-40),
