R = Path("results")


def references():
    out = {}
    for n in ("success03",):
        out[n] = dict(full=stim.Circuit.from_file(str(R / "zz" / f"{n}.full.stim")),
                      inner=stim.Circuit.from_file(str(R / "zz" / f"{n}.inner.stim")),
                      native=None, note="ZZ + X flag, fault distance 3 (previous round's best)")
    out["G4-CX"] = dict(full=stim.Circuit.from_file(str(R / "g4" / "G4-CX.full.stim")),
                        inner=stim.Circuit.from_file(str(R / "g4" / "G4-CX.inner.stim")),
                        native=stim.Circuit.from_file(str(R / "g4" / "G4-native_CZH.inner.stim")),
                        note="Google's as-run double check (Fig. 2), CX form; native = its own CZ + H")
    inner = G6.g4_without_q7()
    out["G4-G6style"] = dict(full=g4.full_for(inner), inner=inner, native=None,
                             note="G4 with q7 unmeasured, as in G6 (Fig. 4 grafting)")
    return out


def emb_of(inner):
    return {q: (int(a), int(b)) for q, (a, b) in C.native_coords(inner).items()}

    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    full, inner = d["full"], d["inner"]
    emb = emb_of(inner)
    r = dict(note=d.get("note", ""), **CMP.structure(inner))

    for mfc in (2, 3):

                              fault_count=v["fault_count"])
    en, _ = CMP.enumerated(full, inner, p_list=(CMP.P0,), mfc=3, detectors_mfc=4)

    for model in ("calibration", "spec"):
        prm = WN.model_params(model, cal, emb)
        noisy_sym, _ = WN.noisy_native(mn.INNER_CIRCUIT, prm, "symmetric")
        noisy_asym, rmap = WN.noisy_native(mn.INNER_CIRCUIT, prm, "asymmetric")

                                readout=rmap)
        r["willow"][model] = dict(rate_T=rate3, rate_T_mfc4=e["T"]["rate"], T_counts=e["T"]["counts"],
                                  acc_enum_detectors=e["detectors"]["acceptance"], mc=mcw,
                                  attempts=1 / mcw["acceptance"],
                                  T_error_per_attempt=rate3 * mcw["acceptance"])
        print(name, model, CMP.kst_now(), f"1 in {1 / rate3:,.0f}", f"acc {mcw['acceptance']:.4f}", flush=True)
    r["runtime_s"] = time.perf_counter() - t0
    return r


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--new", nargs="+", required=True, help="path prefixes of new circuits (.full/.inner.stim)")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="results/continuing_validation.json")
    ap.add_argument("--shots-uniform", type=int, default=10_000_000)
    ap.add_argument("--shots-willow", type=int, default=4_000_000)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    cal = WN.load_calibration()
    ds = {}
    for p in a.new:
        n = Path(p).name
        ds[n] = dict(full=stim.Circuit.from_file(p + ".full.stim"),
                     inner=stim.Circuit.from_file(p + ".inner.stim"), native=None,
                     note=f"continuing-data search ({p})")
    ds.update(references())
    rec = dict(started=CMP.kst_now(), settings=dict(
        uniform="enum.noise.uniformly_depolarize p = 0.001, CX form; MC 10,000,000 shots, kept = no detector",
        willow="willow_noise calibration / spec models, native CZ + H at own Willow positions; enumeration "
               "mfc 4 (table mfc 3); MC 4,000,000 shots, asymmetric readout",
        durations_ns=WN.DUR, reset_error=WN.RESET_ERROR), designs={})
    for n, d in ds.items():
        rec["designs"][n] = validate(n, d, a.shots_uniform, a.shots_willow, cal)
        Path(a.out).write_text(json.dumps(rec, indent=1, default=str))
    rec["finished"] = CMP.kst_now()
    Path(a.out).write_text(json.dumps(rec, indent=1, default=str))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

                              fault_count=v["fault_count"])
    en, _ = CMP.enumerated(full, inner, p_list=(CMP.P0,), mfc=3, detectors_mfc=4)
    e = en[CMP.P0]
    m = load_measurement(full, inner)
    mc = CMP.mc_acceptance(enum.noise.uniformly_depolarize(m.INNER_CIRCUIT, noise_level=CMP.P0),
                           shots_uniform, seed=zlib.crc32(f"{name}cont".encode()))
    r["uniform"] = dict(rate_T_mfc3=r["mfc3"]["rate"]["T"], acc_enum_T=e["T"]["acceptance"],
                        acc_enum_detectors=e["detectors"]["acceptance"], mc=mc,
                        attempts=1 / mc["acceptance"],
                        T_error_per_attempt=r["mfc3"]["rate"]["T"] * mc["acceptance"])
    # realistic Willow noise, native CZ + H at the circuit's own Willow positions
    native = d["native"] if d["native"] is not None else WN.cx_to_native(inner)
    r["native_ticks"] = native.num_ticks
    vn = verify(full, native, max_fault_count=3)
    r["native_uniform_counts_equal"] = vn["T"] == r["mfc3"]["T"] and vn["S"] == r["mfc3"]["S"]
    mn = load_measurement(full, native)
    r["willow"] = {}
    for model in ("calibration", "spec"):
        prm = WN.model_params(model, cal, emb)
        noisy_sym, _ = WN.noisy_native(mn.INNER_CIRCUIT, prm, "symmetric")
        noisy_asym, rmap = WN.noisy_native(mn.INNER_CIRCUIT, prm, "asymmetric")
        en, _ = CMP.enumerated(full, native, mfc=WN.MFC_CHECK, noisy=noisy_sym)
        e = en["custom"]
        rate3 = e["T"]["rate_by_mfc"][3]
        mcw = CMP.mc_acceptance(noisy_asym, shots_willow, seed=zlib.crc32(f"{name}{model}".encode()),
                                readout=rmap)
        r["willow"][model] = dict(rate_T=rate3, rate_T_mfc4=e["T"]["rate"], T_counts=e["T"]["counts"],
                                  acc_enum_detectors=e["detectors"]["acceptance"], mc=mcw,
                                  attempts=1 / mcw["acceptance"],
                                  T_error_per_attempt=rate3 * mcw["acceptance"])
        print(name, model, CMP.kst_now(), f"1 in {1 / rate3:,.0f}", f"acc {mcw['acceptance']:.4f}", flush=True)
    r["runtime_s"] = time.perf_counter() - t0
    return r


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--new", nargs="+", required=True, help="path prefixes of new circuits (.full/.inner.stim)")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="results/continuing_validation.json")
    ap.add_argument("--shots-uniform", type=int, default=10_000_000)
    ap.add_argument("--shots-willow", type=int, default=4_000_000)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    cal = WN.load_calibration()
    ds = {}
    for p in a.new:
        n = Path(p).name
        ds[n] = dict(full=stim.Circuit.from_file(p + ".full.stim"),
                     inner=stim.Circuit.from_file(p + ".inner.stim"), native=None,
                     note=f"continuing-data search ({p})")
    ds.update(references())
    rec = dict(started=CMP.kst_now(), settings=dict(
        uniform="enum.noise.uniformly_depolarize p = 0.001, CX form; MC 10,000,000 shots, kept = no detector",
        willow="willow_noise calibration / spec models, native CZ + H at own Willow positions; enumeration "
               "mfc 4 (table mfc 3); MC 4,000,000 shots, asymmetric readout",
        durations_ns=WN.DUR, reset_error=WN.RESET_ERROR), designs={})
    for n, d in ds.items():
        rec["designs"][n] = validate(n, d, a.shots_uniform, a.shots_willow, cal)
        Path(a.out).write_text(json.dumps(rec, indent=1, default=str))
    rec["finished"] = CMP.kst_now()
    Path(a.out).write_text(json.dumps(rec, indent=1, default=str))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

from nnflags import constraints as C

    "figure.facecolor": "white", "axes.facecolor": "white", "savefig.facecolor": "white",

    for L in lines:
        qs = sorted((q for q in WILLOW if readout_line(q) == L))
        (x0, y0), (x1, y1) = xy(qs[0]), xy(qs[-1])
        ax.plot([x0 + 0.35, x1 - 0.35], [y0 + 0.35, y1 - 0.35], color="#bbbbbb",
                lw=0.6, ls=(0, (3, 3)), zorder=0)
        if line_labels:

                    ha="left", va="bottom", zorder=0)

        (xa, ya), (xb, yb) = xy(a), xy(b)
        ax.plot([xa, xb], [ya, yb], color="#d0d0d0" if faint else "#888888",
                lw=0.8 if faint else 1.0, zorder=1)

    ax.scatter(xs, ys, s=14 if faint else 22, color="#cccccc" if faint else "black", zorder=2,
               linewidths=0)

    import csv
    path = RESULTS / "zz_candidates.csv" if path is None else path
    if not path.exists():
        return []
    rows = [r for r in csv.DictReader(path.open()) if r.get("malignant_T_2") not in (None, "")]
    if successes_only:
        rows = [r for r in rows if r.get("success") == "True"]
    key = lambda r: (int(r["malignant_S_2"] or 0), int(r["n_flags"]), int(r["added_ticks"] or 0),
                     int(r["malignant_T_3"] or 10 ** 6), int(r["id"]))
    return sorted(rows, key=key)


def _circuit_roles(inner, n_flags):
    """data = MPP targets; parity = qubits measured before the final measurement TICK;
    flags = the last n_flags qubits; flag type and control CXs from the gates."""
    from nnflags import zzflags as Z
    data = set(C.find_data_indices(inner))
    layers = C.split_by_ticks(inner)
    meas = {}
    for t, layer in enumerate(layers):
        for op in layer:
            if op.name != "MPP" and stim_gate(op.name).produces_measurements:
                for x in op.targets_copy():
                    meas.setdefault(x.value, []).append(t)
    final = max(t for ts in meas.values() for t in ts)
    parity = {q for q, ts in meas.items() if min(ts) < final}
    nq = inner.num_qubits
    flags = list(range(nq - n_flags, nq))
    _, gates = Z.flag_specs(inner, flags)
    return data, parity, flags, gates

        else:
            ax.plot([xa, xb], [ya, yb], color=BLUE, lw=2.4, zorder=3)

        embs.append(emb)

        ax.text(0.0, 1.01, f"malignant T: {r['malignant_T_1']} / {r['malignant_T_2']} / {r['malignant_T_3']} "
                f"at 1 / 2 / 3 faults; malignant S at <= 2 faults: {r['malignant_S_2']}\n"

                transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=7, va="bottom", ha="left")
    half = max(max(max(p[0] for p in e.values()) - min(p[0] for p in e.values()),

    for ax, e in zip(axes, embs):
        rc = (max(p[0] for p in e.values()) + min(p[0] for p in e.values())) / 2
        cc = (max(p[1] for p in e.values()) + min(p[1] for p in e.values())) / 2
        ax.set_xlim(cc - half, cc + half)
        ax.set_ylim(-rc - half, -rc + half)
    lax = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, :])
    lax.axis("off")
    _zz_legend(lax, anchor=(0.0, 1.0), ncol=4)
    fig.suptitle("Best fault-distance-3 double checks on Willow (0 malignant T configurations with <= 2 "
                 "faults), two flags each", x=0.01, ha="left", fontsize=11, y=0.97)
    fig.text(0.01, 0.02, ZZ_RULE, fontsize=7.2, ha="left", va="bottom")
    save(fig, out, "zz_best_circuits")

]

            ax.text(x0 + 0.45, y0 + 0.45, str(L), fontsize=6, color="#777777",
                    ha="left", va="bottom", zorder=0)
    for a, b in edges():
        (xa, ya), (xb, yb) = xy(a), xy(b)
        ax.plot([xa, xb], [ya, yb], color="#d0d0d0" if faint else "#888888",
                lw=0.8 if faint else 1.0, zorder=1)
    xs, ys = zip(*(xy(q) for q in WILLOW))
    ax.scatter(xs, ys, s=14 if faint else 22, color="#cccccc" if faint else "black", zorder=2,
               linewidths=0)
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    cols = range(min(c for _, c in WILLOW), max(c for _, c in WILLOW) + 1)
    ax.set_xticks(list(cols)[::2], [str(c) for c in list(cols)[::2]])
    ax.set_yticks([-r for r in range(rmin, rmax + 1, 2)],
                  [str(r) for r in range(rmin, rmax + 1, 2)])
    ax.set_xlabel("column c")
    ax.set_ylabel("row r")
    for s in ("top", "right"):
        ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)


def fig_willow_grid(out):
    spec_q, spec_e = load_spec_file()
def _zz_rows(path=None, successes_only=True):
    import csv
    path = RESULTS / "zz_candidates.csv" if path is None else path
    if not path.exists():
        return []
    rows = [r for r in csv.DictReader(path.open()) if r.get("malignant_T_2") not in (None, "")]
    if successes_only:
        rows = [r for r in rows if r.get("success") == "True"]
    key = lambda r: (int(r["malignant_S_2"] or 0), int(r["n_flags"]), int(r["added_ticks"] or 0),
                     int(r["malignant_T_3"] or 10 ** 6), int(r["id"]))
    return sorted(rows, key=key)


def _circuit_roles(inner, n_flags):
    """data = MPP targets; parity = qubits measured before the final measurement TICK;
    flags = the last n_flags qubits; flag type and control CXs from the gates."""
    from nnflags import zzflags as Z
    data = set(C.find_data_indices(inner))
    layers = C.split_by_ticks(inner)
    meas = {}
    for t, layer in enumerate(layers):
        for op in layer:
            if op.name != "MPP" and stim_gate(op.name).produces_measurements:
                for x in op.targets_copy():
                    meas.setdefault(x.value, []).append(t)
    final = max(t for ts in meas.values() for t in ts)
    parity = {q for q, ts in meas.items() if min(ts) < final}
    nq = inner.num_qubits
    flags = list(range(nq - n_flags, nq))
    _, gates = Z.flag_specs(inner, flags)
    return data, parity, flags, gates


def stim_gate(name):
    import stim
    return stim.gate_data(name)


def _draw_zz_circuit(ax, inner, emb, data, parity, flags, gates, hooks=(), label=None):
    draw_willow(ax, faint=True, line_labels=False)
    pairs = {tuple(sorted((a, b))) for _, _, a, b in C.two_qubit_gates(inner)}
    for a, b in sorted(pairs):
        (xa, ya), (xb, yb) = xy(emb[a]), xy(emb[b])
        if a in flags or b in flags:
            f = a if a in flags else b
            col = SKY if gates[f][0][2] == "Z" else ORANGE
            ax.plot([xa, xb], [ya, yb], color=col, lw=2.4, ls=(0, (3, 1.5)), zorder=3)
            q = b if f == a else a
            ts = ",".join(str(t) for t, qq, _ in sorted(gates[f]) if qq == q)
            ax.text((xa + xb) / 2, (ya + yb) / 2, "t" + ts, fontsize=6.2, color="black", ha="center",
                    va="center", zorder=6, bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.12", fc="white", ec=col, lw=0.6))
        else:
            ax.plot([xa, xb], [ya, yb], color=BLUE, lw=2.4, zorder=3)
    for L in sorted({readout_line(emb[q]) for q in parity}):
        _draw_line(ax, L, **PARITY_LINE)
        q0 = max((q for q in parity if readout_line(emb[q]) == L), key=lambda q: emb[q][1])
        x0, y0 = xy(emb[q0])
        ax.text(x0 + 0.75, y0 + 0.55, f"line {L}", fontsize=7, color="#8a5a00", zorder=1)
    for q, p in emb.items():
        x, y = xy(p)
        ec, lw = (VERMILION, 2.6) if q in hooks else ("black", 1.2)
        if q in flags:
            st = ZFLAG_STYLE if gates[q][0][2] == "Z" else XFLAG_STYLE
            ax.scatter([x], [y], **{**st, "edgecolor": ec, "linewidths": lw}, zorder=4)
        elif q in parity:
            ax.scatter([x], [y], s=250, marker="D", facecolor="#f0f0f0", edgecolor=ec, linewidths=lw,
                       hatch="....", zorder=4)
        else:
            ax.scatter([x], [y], s=220, marker="o" if q in data else "s", facecolor="white",
                       edgecolor=ec, linewidths=lw, zorder=4)
        ax.text(x, y, str(q), ha="center", va="center", fontsize=7.2, zorder=5,
                fontweight="bold" if q in data else "normal",
                bbox=dict(boxstyle="circle,pad=0.02", fc="white", ec="none") if q in parity or q in flags
                else None)
    zoom(ax, emb, pad=1.3)
    if label:
        ax.set_title(label, loc="left", fontsize=9, pad=44)


def _zz_legend(ax, anchor=(0.0, -0.1), ncol=3):
    h = [Line2D([], [], marker="o", ls="", mfc="white", mec="black", markersize=9, label="data qubit"),
         Line2D([], [], marker="s", ls="", mfc="white", mec="black", markersize=8, label="ancilla"),
         Line2D([], [], marker="D", ls="", mfc="#f0f0f0", mec="black", markersize=8,
                label="parity qubit (mid-circuit MRX)"),
         Line2D([], [], color=BLUE, lw=2.4, label="CX of the double check"),
         Line2D([], [], **PARITY_LINE, label="readout line r + c of the parity qubit"),
         Line2D([], [], marker="^", ls="", mfc="#e8e8e8", mec="black", markersize=9,
                label="Z flag (R, CX q->f, M)"),
         Line2D([], [], color=SKY, lw=2.4, ls=(0, (3, 1.5)), label="Z-flag CX, label = its TICKs"),
         Line2D([], [], marker="v", ls="", mfc="#f6e3b4", mec="black", markersize=9,
                label="X flag (RX, CX f->q, MX)"),
         Line2D([], [], color=ORANGE, lw=2.4, ls=(0, (3, 1.5)), label="X-flag CX, label = its TICKs"),
         Line2D([], [], marker="o", ls="", mfc="white", mec=VERMILION, mew=2.6, markersize=9,
                label="X-hook qubit of the unflagged base")]
    ax.legend(handles=h, loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=anchor, ncol=ncol, fontsize=7.2)


def _base_design(name):
    from nnflags import search_zzflags as S
    from nnflags import zzflags as Z
    if name == "G4":
        return Z.design_g4()
    t = next(x for x in S.tasks({}) if x[0] == name)
    return Z.design_from_option1(t[1], t[2], name=name)


def fig_zz_best_circuits(out, k=3):
    import stim
    from nnflags import zzflags as Z
    rows = _zz_rows()[:k]
    if not rows:
        return
    n = len(rows)
    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(5.6 * n, 8.2))
    gs = fig.add_gridspec(2, n, height_ratios=[5.2, 1.0], left=0.05, right=0.98, top=0.8, bottom=0.08,
                          wspace=0.25, hspace=0.25)
    axes = [fig.add_subplot(gs[0, i]) for i in range(n)]
    embs = []
    for ax, r in zip(axes, rows):
        inner = stim.Circuit.from_file(r["stim_file"])
        emb = {q: (int(a), int(b)) for q, (a, b) in C.native_coords(inner).items()}
        embs.append(emb)
        data, parity, flags, gates = _circuit_roles(inner, int(r["n_flags"]))
        hooks = set(Z.hook_qubits(_base_design(r["base"])))
        _draw_zz_circuit(ax, inner, emb, data, parity, flags, gates, hooks=hooks,
                         label=f"{Path(r['stim_file']).name.split('.')[0]} (base {r['base']}): "
                               f"{r['n_flags']} flags, +{r['added_ticks']} TICKs")
        ax.text(0.0, 1.01, f"malignant T: {r['malignant_T_1']} / {r['malignant_T_2']} / {r['malignant_T_3']} "
                f"at 1 / 2 / 3 faults; malignant S at <= 2 faults: {r['malignant_S_2']}\n"
                f"T error per kept shot: 0 (max_fault_count 2), {one_in(float(r['ler_T_mfc3']))} "
                f"(max_fault_count 3)\n{r['n_qubits']} qubits, {r['n_cx']} CX, max degree {r['max_degree']}",
                transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=7, va="bottom", ha="left")
    half = max(max(max(p[0] for p in e.values()) - min(p[0] for p in e.values()),
                   max(p[1] for p in e.values()) - min(p[1] for p in e.values())) for e in embs) / 2 + 1.0
    for ax, e in zip(axes, embs):
        rc = (max(p[0] for p in e.values()) + min(p[0] for p in e.values())) / 2
        cc = (max(p[1] for p in e.values()) + min(p[1] for p in e.values())) / 2
        ax.set_xlim(cc - half, cc + half)
        ax.set_ylim(-rc - half, -rc + half)
    lax = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, :])
    lax.axis("off")
    _zz_legend(lax, anchor=(0.0, 1.0), ncol=4)
    fig.suptitle("Best fault-distance-3 double checks on Willow (0 malignant T configurations with <= 2 "
                 "faults), two flags each", x=0.01, ha="left", fontsize=11, y=0.97)
    fig.text(0.01, 0.02, ZZ_RULE, fontsize=7.2, ha="left", va="bottom")
    save(fig, out, "zz_best_circuits")

"""Figures of the continuing-data search round (RESULTS_continuing_search.md). PNG only.

    .venv/bin/python -m nnflags.plots_continuing [--out figures]

  * continuing_circuits.png: Google's G6 cultivation patch and the best new
    circuit(s) on Willow; readout lines r + c of data qubits (blue bands) and of
    measured qubits (orange dashed bands) drawn separately, roles from the MPP
    targets and from the measurements.
  * continuing_comparison.png: G4, G4 as run in G6 (q7 unmeasured), success03 and
    the new best: malignant T at 2 / 3 faults, continuing-data conflicts, T error
    per kept shot (uniform p = 0.1 % and Willow calibration model).
"""
import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import stim
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
from matplotlib.ticker import FixedLocator, FuncFormatter, NullLocator

from nnflags import constraints as C
from nnflags import g6_continuing as G6
from nnflags.plots import (BLUE, GREEN, GREY, ORANGE, SKY, VERMILION, draw_willow, one_in, save, xy)
from nnflags.willow import readout_line

R = Path("results")


def roles(inner):
    """data (MPP targets), measured non-data qubits, mid-measured (parity) qubits,
    unmeasured ancillas, flags {q: 'Z'|'X'} (qubits whose every 2q gate is a probe:
    R + CX q->f + M or RX + CX f->q + MX, measured only in the final layer)."""
    data = set(C.find_data_indices(inner))
    meas_t = {}
    for t, layer in enumerate(C.split_by_ticks(inner)):
        for name, qs, gd in C._hardware_ops(layer):
            if gd.produces_measurements:
                for q in qs:
                    meas_t.setdefault(q, []).append((t, name))
    final = max(t for v in meas_t.values() for t, _ in v)
    used = {q for _, _, a, b in C.two_qubit_gates(inner) for q in (a, b)}
    parity = {q for q, v in meas_t.items() if min(t for t, _ in v) < final}
    unmeasured = used - data - set(meas_t)
    return data, set(meas_t) - data, parity, unmeasured


def flag_types(inner, n_flags):
    nq = inner.num_qubits
    out = {}
    for f in range(nq - n_flags, nq):
        g = [(a, b) for _, _, a, b in C.two_qubit_gates(inner) if f in (a, b)]
        out[f] = "Z" if g and g[0][1] == f else "X"
    return out


def band(ax, L, lo, hi, kind):
    xs = [lo, hi]
    ys = [x - L for x in xs]
    if kind == "data":
        ax.plot(xs, ys, color=BLUE, lw=11, alpha=0.16, solid_capstyle="butt", zorder=0.5)
    else:
        ax.plot(xs, ys, color=ORANGE, lw=3.0, alpha=0.9, ls=(0, (4, 3)), zorder=0.5)


def draw_circuit(ax, inner, emb, flags=None, title=""):
    flags = flags or {}
    data, measured, parity, unmeasured = roles(inner)
    draw_willow(ax, faint=True, line_labels=False)
    xs = [xy(p)[0] for p in emb.values()]
    lo, hi = min(xs) - 2.5, max(xs) + 2.5
    dl = sorted({readout_line(emb[q]) for q in data})
    ml = sorted({readout_line(emb[q]) for q in measured})
    for L in dl:
        band(ax, L, lo, hi, "data")
    for L in ml:
        band(ax, L, lo, hi, "measured")
    pairs = {tuple(sorted((a, b))) for _, _, a, b in C.two_qubit_gates(inner)}
    for a, b in sorted(pairs):
        (xa, ya), (xb, yb) = xy(emb[a]), xy(emb[b])
        f = a if a in flags else b if b in flags else None
        if f is None:
            ax.plot([xa, xb], [ya, yb], color="black", lw=1.8, zorder=3)
        else:
            ax.plot([xa, xb], [ya, yb], color=SKY if flags[f] == "Z" else VERMILION, lw=2.0,
                    ls=(0, (3, 1.5)), zorder=3)
    for q, p in emb.items():
        if q not in data | measured | unmeasured:
            continue
        x, y = xy(p)
        if q in flags:
            ax.scatter([x], [y], s=210, marker="^" if flags[q] == "Z" else "v", facecolor="#e8e8e8",
                       edgecolor="black", linewidths=1.2, zorder=4)
        elif q in parity:
            ax.scatter([x], [y], s=230, marker="D", facecolor=ORANGE, edgecolor="black", linewidths=1.2,
                       hatch="....", zorder=4)
        elif q in measured:
            ax.scatter([x], [y], s=200, marker="s", facecolor="#fbe3b0", edgecolor="black",
                       linewidths=1.2, zorder=4)
        elif q in unmeasured:
            ax.scatter([x], [y], s=200, marker="s", facecolor="white", edgecolor="black",
                       linewidths=1.2, linestyle="--", zorder=4)
        else:
            ax.scatter([x], [y], s=200, marker="o", facecolor="#cfe3f3", edgecolor="black",
                       linewidths=1.2, zorder=4)
        ax.text(x, y, str(q), ha="center", va="center", fontsize=6.5, zorder=5)
    ys = [xy(p)[1] for p in emb.values()]
    half = max(max(xs) - min(xs), max(ys) - min(ys)) / 2 + 1.4
    cx, cy = (max(xs) + min(xs)) / 2, (max(ys) + min(ys)) / 2
    ax.set_xlim(cx - half, cx + half)
    ax.set_ylim(cy - half, cy + half)
    ax.set_title(title, loc="left", fontsize=8.5)
    ax.text(0.0, -0.13, f"data lines r + c: {', '.join(map(str, dl))}\n"
            f"measured-qubit lines: {', '.join(map(str, ml))}  (disjoint: "
            f"{'yes' if not set(dl) & set(ml) else 'NO'})", transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=7.2, va="top")


def legend(fig):
    h = [Line2D([], [], marker="o", ls="", mfc="#cfe3f3", mec="black", markersize=9, label="data qubit (continues)"),
         Line2D([], [], marker="D", ls="", mfc=ORANGE, mec="black", markersize=8, label="parity root (mid-check readout)"),
         Line2D([], [], marker="s", ls="", mfc="#fbe3b0", mec="black", markersize=8, label="ancilla, read out at the end"),
         Line2D([], [], marker="s", ls="", mfc="white", mec="black", markersize=8, label="ancilla never read out (reset only)"),
         Line2D([], [], marker="^", ls="", mfc="#e8e8e8", mec="black", markersize=9, label="Z flag"),
         Line2D([], [], marker="v", ls="", mfc="#e8e8e8", mec="black", markersize=9, label="X flag"),
         Line2D([], [], color=BLUE, lw=9, alpha=0.25, label="readout line of a data qubit"),
         Line2D([], [], color=ORANGE, lw=3, ls=(0, (4, 3)), label="readout line of a measured qubit"),
         Line2D([], [], color="black", lw=1.8, label="CX / CZ of the double check"),
         Line2D([], [], color=SKY, lw=2, ls=(0, (3, 1.5)), label="Z-flag CX"),
         Line2D([], [], color=VERMILION, lw=2, ls=(0, (3, 1.5)), label="X-flag CX")]
    fig.legend(handles=h, loc="lower left", ncol=4, fontsize=7.2, frameon=False, bbox_to_anchor=(0.01, 0.0))


def fig_circuits(out, new):
    """new = [(label, inner stim path, n_flags, stats text)]"""
    g, emb6 = G6.load_g6()
    data6 = G6.tagged_targets(g, "T_gate")
    cult = G6.sub_circuit(g, 31, 57)   # double check + its readout (TICKs 31-56)
    # the G6 double check as an inner-like circuit with an MPP marker on the data, so that
    # roles() finds the data
    c6 = stim.Circuit()
    for q, p in emb6.items():
        if q in set(data6) | {3, 9, 11, 12, 19}:
            c6.append("QUBIT_COORDS", [q], p)
    c6.append("MPP", [x for q in data6 for x in (stim.target_x(q), stim.target_combiner())][:-1])
    c6.append("TICK")
    c6 += cult
    e6 = {q: p for q, p in emb6.items() if q in set(data6) | {3, 9, 11, 12, 19}}
    n = 1 + len(new)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, n, figsize=(4.6 * n, 6.0))
    axes = list(axes) if n > 1 else [axes]
    draw_circuit(axes[0], c6, e6, title="Google G6 (Rosenfeld et al. Fig. 4):\ncultivation double check, as run")
    for ax, (label, path, nf, stats) in zip(axes[1:], new):
        inner = stim.Circuit.from_file(path)
        emb = {q: (int(a), int(b)) for q, (a, b) in C.native_coords(inner).items()}
        draw_circuit(ax, inner, emb, flags=flag_types(inner, nf), title=label)
        ax.text(0.0, -0.25, stats, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=7.2, va="top")
    fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.04, right=0.99, top=0.9, bottom=0.3, wspace=0.18)
    legend(fig)
    fig.suptitle("Readout lines when the data continue: data lines (blue) and measured-qubit lines "
                 "(orange) must be disjoint", x=0.01, ha="left", fontsize=10)
    save(fig, out, "continuing_circuits")


def fig_comparison(out, val, names, labels):
    D = val["designs"]
    styles = [dict(facecolor=VERMILION, hatch="////"), dict(facecolor=ORANGE, hatch="\\\\\\\\"),
              dict(facecolor=GREY, hatch="xx"), dict(facecolor=GREEN, hatch=""),
              dict(facecolor=SKY, hatch=".."), dict(facecolor=BLUE, hatch="--")]
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(14, 3.9))
    x = list(range(len(names)))

    def bars(ax, vals, title, ylabel, fmt=str):
        rs = ax.bar(x, vals, width=0.7, edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.6)
        for r, st in zip(rs, styles):
            r.set_facecolor(st["facecolor"])
            r.set_hatch(st["hatch"])
        for xi, v in zip(x, vals):
            ax.text(xi, v, fmt(v), ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=7)
        ax.set_xticks(x, labels, rotation=30, ha="right", fontsize=7.5)
        ax.set_title(title, fontsize=9, loc="left")
        ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
        ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(lambda v, _p: f"{v:,.0f}"))

    bars(axes[0], [D[n]["mfc3"]["T"][2]["malignant"] for n in names], "(a) malignant T, 2 faults",
         "configurations")
    bars(axes[1], [D[n]["mfc3"]["T"][3]["malignant"] for n in names], "(b) malignant T, 3 faults",
         "configurations")
    bars(axes[2], [D[n]["continuing"] for n in names], "(c) continuing-data conflicts", "violations")
    ax = axes[3]
    w = 0.38
    u = [1 / D[n]["uniform"]["rate_T_mfc3"] for n in names]
    c = [1 / D[n]["willow"]["calibration"]["rate_T"] for n in names]
    r1 = ax.bar([i - w / 2 for i in x], u, width=w, facecolor=BLUE, edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.6,
                label="uniform p = 0.1 %, CX")
    r2 = ax.bar([i + w / 2 for i in x], c, width=w, facecolor=ORANGE, hatch="////", edgecolor="black",
                linewidth=0.6, label="Willow calibration, CZ + H")
    ax.set_yscale("log")
    ticks = [10_000, 100_000, 1_000_000, 10_000_000]
    ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(FixedLocator(ticks))
    ax.yaxis.set_minor_locator(NullLocator())
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(lambda v, _p: f"1 in {v:,.0f}"))
    ax.set_ylim(8_000, 30_000_000)
    ax.set_xticks(x, labels, rotation=30, ha="right", fontsize=7.5)
    ax.set_title("(d) T error per kept shot (mfc 3)", fontsize=9, loc="left")
    ax.set_ylabel("higher is better")
    ax.legend(fontsize=7, loc="upper left")
    fig.tight_layout()
    save(fig, out, "continuing_comparison")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="figures")
    ap.add_argument("--val", default="results/continuing_validation.json")
    ap.add_argument("--new", nargs="*", default=[], help="label=path=n_flags entries")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    out = Path(a.out)

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import stim
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
from matplotlib.ticker import FixedLocator, FuncFormatter, NullLocator

from nnflags import constraints as C
from nnflags import g6_continuing as G6
from nnflags.plots import (BLUE, GREEN, GREY, ORANGE, SKY, VERMILION, draw_willow, one_in, save, xy)
from nnflags.willow import readout_line

R = Path("results")


def roles(inner):
    """data (MPP targets), measured non-data qubits, mid-measured (parity) qubits,
    unmeasured ancillas, flags {q: 'Z'|'X'} (qubits whose every 2q gate is a probe:
    R + CX q->f + M or RX + CX f->q + MX, measured only in the final layer)."""
    data = set(C.find_data_indices(inner))
    meas_t = {}

        for name, qs, gd in C._hardware_ops(layer):
            if gd.produces_measurements:
                for q in qs:
                    meas_t.setdefault(q, []).append((t, name))

    parity = {q for q, v in meas_t.items() if min(t for t, _ in v) < final}
    unmeasured = used - data - set(meas_t)
    return data, set(meas_t) - data, parity, unmeasured


def flag_types(inner, n_flags):
    nq = inner.num_qubits
    out = {}
    for f in range(nq - n_flags, nq):
        g = [(a, b) for _, _, a, b in C.two_qubit_gates(inner) if f in (a, b)]
        out[f] = "Z" if g and g[0][1] == f else "X"
    return out


def band(ax, L, lo, hi, kind):
    xs = [lo, hi]
    ys = [x - L for x in xs]
    if kind == "data":

    else:
        ax.plot(xs, ys, color=ORANGE, lw=3.0, alpha=0.9, ls=(0, (4, 3)), zorder=0.5)

    flags = flags or {}

    lo, hi = min(xs) - 2.5, max(xs) + 2.5

    ml = sorted({readout_line(emb[q]) for q in measured})
    for L in dl:
        band(ax, L, lo, hi, "data")
    for L in ml:
        band(ax, L, lo, hi, "measured")

                       linewidths=1.2, zorder=4)
        elif q in unmeasured:

                       linewidths=1.2, linestyle="--", zorder=4)
        else:

                       linewidths=1.2, zorder=4)

    cx, cy = (max(xs) + min(xs)) / 2, (max(ys) + min(ys)) / 2

    ax.set_ylim(cy - half, cy + half)

            f"measured-qubit lines: {', '.join(map(str, ml))}  (disjoint: "
            f"{'yes' if not set(dl) & set(ml) else 'NO'})", transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=7.2, va="top")


def legend(fig):

         Line2D([], [], marker="D", ls="", mfc=ORANGE, mec="black", markersize=8, label="parity root (mid-check readout)"),
         Line2D([], [], marker="s", ls="", mfc="#fbe3b0", mec="black", markersize=8, label="ancilla, read out at the end"),
         Line2D([], [], marker="s", ls="", mfc="white", mec="black", markersize=8, label="ancilla never read out (reset only)"),
         Line2D([], [], marker="^", ls="", mfc="#e8e8e8", mec="black", markersize=9, label="Z flag"),
         Line2D([], [], marker="v", ls="", mfc="#e8e8e8", mec="black", markersize=9, label="X flag"),
         Line2D([], [], color=BLUE, lw=9, alpha=0.25, label="readout line of a data qubit"),
         Line2D([], [], color=ORANGE, lw=3, ls=(0, (4, 3)), label="readout line of a measured qubit"),
         Line2D([], [], color="black", lw=1.8, label="CX / CZ of the double check"),
         Line2D([], [], color=SKY, lw=2, ls=(0, (3, 1.5)), label="Z-flag CX"),
         Line2D([], [], color=VERMILION, lw=2, ls=(0, (3, 1.5)), label="X-flag CX")]
    fig.legend(handles=h, loc="lower left", ncol=4, fontsize=7.2, frameon=False, bbox_to_anchor=(0.01, 0.0))

    lab = {"G4-CX": "G4 (as run)", "G4-G6style": "G4, q7 unread\n(G6 style)", "success03": "success03"}

        emb = {q: (int(a), int(b)) for q, (a, b) in C.native_coords(inner).items()}
        draw_circuit(ax, inner, emb, flags=flag_types(inner, nf), title=label)
        ax.text(0.0, -0.25, stats, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=7.2, va="top")
    fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.04, right=0.99, top=0.9, bottom=0.3, wspace=0.18)
    legend(fig)
    fig.suptitle("Readout lines when the data continue: data lines (blue) and measured-qubit lines "
                 "(orange) must be disjoint", x=0.01, ha="left", fontsize=10)
    save(fig, out, "continuing_circuits")


def fig_comparison(out, val, names, labels):
    D = val["designs"]
    styles = [dict(facecolor=VERMILION, hatch="////"), dict(facecolor=ORANGE, hatch="\\\\\\\\"),
              dict(facecolor=GREY, hatch="xx"), dict(facecolor=GREEN, hatch=""),
              dict(facecolor=SKY, hatch=".."), dict(facecolor=BLUE, hatch="--")]
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(14, 3.9))
    x = list(range(len(names)))

    def bars(ax, vals, title, ylabel, fmt=str):
        rs = ax.bar(x, vals, width=0.7, edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.6)
        for r, st in zip(rs, styles):
            r.set_facecolor(st["facecolor"])
            r.set_hatch(st["hatch"])
        for xi, v in zip(x, vals):
            ax.text(xi, v, fmt(v), ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=7)
        ax.set_xticks(x, labels, rotation=30, ha="right", fontsize=7.5)
        ax.set_title(title, fontsize=9, loc="left")
        ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
        ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(lambda v, _p: f"{v:,.0f}"))

    bars(axes[0], [D[n]["mfc3"]["T"][2]["malignant"] for n in names], "(a) malignant T, 2 faults",
         "configurations")
    bars(axes[1], [D[n]["mfc3"]["T"][3]["malignant"] for n in names], "(b) malignant T, 3 faults",
         "configurations")
    bars(axes[2], [D[n]["continuing"] for n in names], "(c) continuing-data conflicts", "violations")
    ax = axes[3]
    w = 0.38
    u = [1 / D[n]["uniform"]["rate_T_mfc3"] for n in names]
    c = [1 / D[n]["willow"]["calibration"]["rate_T"] for n in names]
    r1 = ax.bar([i - w / 2 for i in x], u, width=w, facecolor=BLUE, edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.6,
                label="uniform p = 0.1 %, CX")
    r2 = ax.bar([i + w / 2 for i in x], c, width=w, facecolor=ORANGE, hatch="////", edgecolor="black",
                linewidth=0.6, label="Willow calibration, CZ + H")
    ax.set_yscale("log")
    ticks = [10_000, 100_000, 1_000_000, 10_000_000]
    ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(FixedLocator(ticks))
    ax.yaxis.set_minor_locator(NullLocator())
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(lambda v, _p: f"1 in {v:,.0f}"))
    ax.set_ylim(8_000, 30_000_000)
    ax.set_xticks(x, labels, rotation=30, ha="right", fontsize=7.5)
    ax.set_title("(d) T error per kept shot (mfc 3)", fontsize=9, loc="left")
    ax.set_ylabel("higher is better")
    ax.legend(fontsize=7, loc="upper left")
    fig.tight_layout()
    save(fig, out, "continuing_comparison")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="figures")
    ap.add_argument("--val", default="results/continuing_validation.json")
    ap.add_argument("--new", nargs="*", default=[], help="label=path=n_flags entries")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    out = Path(a.out)
    val = json.loads(Path(a.val).read_text())
    new = []
    for s in a.new:
        label, path, nf = s.split("=")
        name = Path(path).name.split(".")[0]
        d = val["designs"].get(name)
        stats = ""
        if d:
            stats = (f"malignant T at 1 / 2 / 3 faults: {d['mfc3']['T'][1]['malignant']} / "
                     f"{d['mfc3']['T'][2]['malignant']} / {d['mfc3']['T'][3]['malignant']}\n"
                     f"T error per kept shot (p = 0.1 %, mfc 3): {one_in(d['uniform']['rate_T_mfc3'])}\n"
                     f"{d['qubits']} qubits, {d['n_2q']} CX, continuing conflicts {d['continuing']}, "
                     f"strict {sum(d['strict'].values())}")
        new.append((label, path, int(nf), stats))
    fig_circuits(out, new)
    names = [n for n in val["designs"]]
    order = ["G4-CX", "G4-G6style", "success03"] + [n for n in names if n not in ("G4-CX", "G4-G6style", "success03")]
    lab = {"G4-CX": "G4 (as run)", "G4-G6style": "G4, q7 unread\n(G6 style)", "success03": "success03"}
    fig_comparison(out, val, order, [lab.get(n, n) for n in order])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""QVM checks (E1-E4 of RESULTS_qvm.md) for circuits of the continuing-data search round.

and the results directory is redirected to qvm-google/results/continuing/.

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
import qvm_willow as QW  # noqa: E402

RES = HERE / "results" / "continuing"


def register(spec: str) -> str:
    name, prefix = spec.split("=")
    QW.DESIGNS[name] = (ROOT / f"{prefix}.full.stim", ROOT / f"{prefix}.inner.stim", "CX",
                        "continuing-data search: fault distance 3, data lines disjoint from measured lines")
    return name


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("exp", choices=["e1", "e2", "e3", "e4"])
    ap.add_argument("--design", required=True, help="NAME=path prefix of .full/.inner.stim")
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=12)
    ap.add_argument("--random-pairs", type=int, default=2000)
    ap.add_argument("--shots", type=int, default=2_000_000)
    ap.add_argument("--chunk", type=int, default=5000)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    os.chdir(ROOT)
    RES.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    QW.RES = RES
    name = register(a.design)
    if a.exp == "e1":
        dev = QW.device()
        out = dict(started=QW.kst_now(), processor=QW.PROCESSOR, designs={name: QW.e1_design(name, dev)})
        from nnflags import constraints as C
        d = QW.load_design(name)
        out["designs"][name]["continuing_data_violations"] = len(
            C.continuing_data_violations(d.inner_src, d.pos, d.data))
        QW._dump(out, RES / f"e1_{name}.json")
    elif a.exp == "e2":
        QW._dump(dict(started=QW.kst_now(), designs={name: QW.e2_design(name)}), RES / f"e2_{name}.json")
    elif a.exp == "e3":
        QW._dump(QW.run_e3(a.random_pairs, a.workers, designs=[name]), RES / f"e3_{name}.json")
    elif a.exp == "e4":
        res = QW.run_e4({name: a.shots}, a.chunk, a.workers, outdir=RES / "e4_chunks")
        QW._dump(dict(updated=QW.kst_now(), chunk=a.chunk, results=res), RES / f"e4_{name}.json")
        for n, s in res.items():
            print(n, s["shots"], f"{100 * s['acceptance']:.3f} %", s["logical_error_given_code"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Evidence for the continuing-data search: what the surviving malignant 2-fault T
pairs of the best 2-flag circuits are, and whether ONE more flag (a third; not
built, analysis only) could separate them, with and without the line rules.

For each saved best circuit (inner + full stim with Willow QUBIT_COORDS):
  * malignant pairs (zzflags.malignant_pairs) and their events (Pauli type of each
    fault: X-type = has X / Y on some qubit, Z-only);
  * for each pair, the number of (basis, control set) single flags that separate it
    (GF(2) test, zzflags.Coverage.system), over all control sets of tree qubits
    (same colour, tree degree <= 3), and how many of those have a free Willow point
    adjacent to all controls that is not on a data line (continuing-data rule) and,
    if the flag is live at the mid check, not on a root line (strict rule).

    .venv/bin/python -m nnflags.continuing_evidence results/continuing/best_s1_0 ...
"""
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import stim

from nnflags import constraints as C
from nnflags import search_zzflags as SZ
from nnflags import zzflags as Z
from nnflags.continuing_data import data_qubits
from nnflags.willow import WILLOW, neighbours, readout_line


def plaquettes_from_full(full):
    out = []
    for inst in full:
        if inst.name == "MPP":
            ts = [t for t in inst.targets_copy() if not t.is_combiner]
            if len(ts) == 4 and all(t.is_z_target for t in ts):
                out.append(tuple(t.value for t in ts))
    return tuple(out)


def evidence(prefix):
    inner = stim.Circuit.from_file(prefix + ".inner.stim")
    full = stim.Circuit.from_file(prefix + ".full.stim")
    emb = {q: (int(a), int(b)) for q, (a, b) in C.native_coords(inner).items()}
    data = sorted(data_qubits(inner))
    d = Z.Design(Path(prefix).name, inner, (plaquettes_from_full(full), (), (), tuple(data)), emb)
    flags = [q for q in d.qubits if q in emb and all(q in (a, b) and (
        (b == q) or (a == q)) for _, _, a, b in C.two_qubit_gates(inner) if q in (a, b))]
    # flags = qubits measured only in the final layer whose every partner is a tree qubit and
    # which are not in the MPP / not ancillas of the fold (they are the highest indices)
    nf = sum(1 for q in d.qubits if q >= max(data) + 1 and q not in d.mid_measured) and 0
    pairs, events, _, _ = Z.malignant_pairs(d, inner, full)
    tree_q = [q for q in d.qubits if q < inner.num_qubits]
    pa = Z.ProbeAnalysis(d, controls=tree_q)
    cov = Z.Coverage(pa, pairs, events)
    dl = {readout_line(emb[q]) for q in data}
    rl = {readout_line(emb[q]) for q in d.mid_measured}
    used = set(emb.values())
    mid = d.mid_ticks[0] if d.mid_ticks else 10 ** 9
    out = dict(file=prefix, pairs=[list(p) for p in pairs], data_lines=sorted(dl), root_lines=sorted(rl),
               per_pair=[])
    for i, (a, b) in enumerate(pairs):
        kinds = []
        for f in (a, b):
            has_x = any(any(ps[q] in (1, 2) for q in range(len(ps))) for _, ps in events[f])
            kinds.append("X-type" if has_x else "Z-only")
        sep = {"Z": [0, 0], "X": [0, 0]}
        for basis in ("Z", "X"):
            for qs in SZ.control_sets(d, tree_q):
                cols = [k for k, p in enumerate(pa.probes) if p.q in qs and p.basis == basis]
                if not cols or Z.solve_gf2(cov.system(cols, [i]), len(cols)) is None:
                    continue
                sep[basis][0] += 1
                pts = set(neighbours(emb[qs[0]]))
                for q in qs[1:]:
                    pts &= set(neighbours(emb[q]))
                live = basis == "X"  # a Z flag can start after the mid check (dormant there)
                ok = [p for p in pts if p in WILLOW and p not in used and readout_line(p) not in dl
                      and not (live and readout_line(p) in rl)]
                sep[basis][1] += bool(ok)
        out["per_pair"].append(dict(pair=[a, b], fault_types=kinds,
                                    events=[[(t, str(ps)) for t, ps in events[f][:3]] for f in (a, b)],
                                    single_flag_sets={k: dict(any=v[0], placeable=v[1]) for k, v in sep.items()}))
    return out


if __name__ == "__main__":
    res = [evidence(p) for p in sys.argv[1:]]
    Path("results/continuing_evidence.json").write_text(json.dumps(res, indent=1, default=str))
    for r in res:
        print(r["file"], "pairs", len(r["pairs"]))
        for pp in r["per_pair"]:
            print("  ", pp["pair"], pp["fault_types"], pp["single_flag_sets"])

  * malignant pairs (zzflags.malignant_pairs) and their events (Pauli type of each
    fault: X-type = has X / Y on some qubit, Z-only);
  * for each pair, the number of (basis, control set) single flags that separate it
    (GF(2) test, zzflags.Coverage.system), over all control sets of tree qubits
    (same colour, tree degree <= 3), and how many of those have a free Willow point
    adjacent to all controls that is not on a data line (continuing-data rule) and,
    if the flag is live at the mid check, not on a root line (strict rule).

"""
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import stim

from nnflags import constraints as C
from nnflags import search_zzflags as SZ
from nnflags import zzflags as Z
from nnflags.continuing_data import data_qubits
from nnflags.willow import WILLOW, neighbours, readout_line


def plaquettes_from_full(full):
    out = []
    for inst in full:
        if inst.name == "MPP":
            ts = [t for t in inst.targets_copy() if not t.is_combiner]
            if len(ts) == 4 and all(t.is_z_target for t in ts):
                out.append(tuple(t.value for t in ts))
    return tuple(out)


def evidence(prefix):
    inner = stim.Circuit.from_file(prefix + ".inner.stim")
    full = stim.Circuit.from_file(prefix + ".full.stim")
    emb = {q: (int(a), int(b)) for q, (a, b) in C.native_coords(inner).items()}
    data = sorted(data_qubits(inner))
    d = Z.Design(Path(prefix).name, inner, (plaquettes_from_full(full), (), (), tuple(data)), emb)
    flags = [q for q in d.qubits if q in emb and all(q in (a, b) and (
        (b == q) or (a == q)) for _, _, a, b in C.two_qubit_gates(inner) if q in (a, b))]
    # flags = qubits measured only in the final layer whose every partner is a tree qubit and
    # which are not in the MPP / not ancillas of the fold (they are the highest indices)
    nf = sum(1 for q in d.qubits if q >= max(data) + 1 and q not in d.mid_measured) and 0
    pairs, events, _, _ = Z.malignant_pairs(d, inner, full)
    tree_q = [q for q in d.qubits if q < inner.num_qubits]
    pa = Z.ProbeAnalysis(d, controls=tree_q)
    cov = Z.Coverage(pa, pairs, events)
    dl = {readout_line(emb[q]) for q in data}
    rl = {readout_line(emb[q]) for q in d.mid_measured}
    used = set(emb.values())
    mid = d.mid_ticks[0] if d.mid_ticks else 10 ** 9
    out = dict(file=prefix, pairs=[list(p) for p in pairs], data_lines=sorted(dl), root_lines=sorted(rl),
               per_pair=[])
    for i, (a, b) in enumerate(pairs):
        kinds = []
        for f in (a, b):
            has_x = any(any(ps[q] in (1, 2) for q in range(len(ps))) for _, ps in events[f])
            kinds.append("X-type" if has_x else "Z-only")
        sep = {"Z": [0, 0], "X": [0, 0]}
        for basis in ("Z", "X"):
            for qs in SZ.control_sets(d, tree_q):
                cols = [k for k, p in enumerate(pa.probes) if p.q in qs and p.basis == basis]
                if not cols or Z.solve_gf2(cov.system(cols, [i]), len(cols)) is None:
                    continue
                sep[basis][0] += 1
                pts = set(neighbours(emb[qs[0]]))
                for q in qs[1:]:
                    pts &= set(neighbours(emb[q]))
                live = basis == "X"  # a Z flag can start after the mid check (dormant there)
                ok = [p for p in pts if p in WILLOW and p not in used and readout_line(p) not in dl
                      and not (live and readout_line(p) in rl)]
                sep[basis][1] += bool(ok)
        out["per_pair"].append(dict(pair=[a, b], fault_types=kinds,
                                    events=[[(t, str(ps)) for t, ps in events[f][:3]] for f in (a, b)],
                                    single_flag_sets={k: dict(any=v[0], placeable=v[1]) for k, v in sep.items()}))
    return out


if __name__ == "__main__":
    res = [evidence(p) for p in sys.argv[1:]]
    Path("results/continuing_evidence.json").write_text(json.dumps(res, indent=1, default=str))
    for r in res:
        print(r["file"], "pairs", len(r["pairs"]))
        for pp in r["per_pair"]:
            print("  ", pp["pair"], pp["fault_types"], pp["single_flag_sets"])

def cover_stats(task):
    """For one abstract key: does a 2-cover of its malignant base pairs by two single-flag
    coverage sets exist (a) abstractly (any same-colour control set, no geometry) and
    (b) with both flags placeable under the line rules on some embedding of the key?
    Also: can ONE flag cover everything, and the minimum number of flags of a greedy
    set cover (abstract and placeable), capped at 4."""
    from nnflags import search_continuing as SC
    key, insts, lab = task
    d, lay = SC.design_for(key, insts[0], tuple(lab))
    placer = SC.Placer(insts)
    tree_q = list(d.qubits)
    pa = Z.ProbeAnalysis(d, controls=tree_q)
    pairs, events, _, _ = Z.malignant_pairs(d)
    n = len(pairs)
    cov = Z.Coverage(pa, pairs, events)
    real = placer.realisability([])
    full = (1 << n) - 1
    masks = {"abstract": [], "placeable": []}
    for basis in ("Z", "X"):
        for qs in SZ.control_sets(d, tree_q):
            cols = [k for k, p in enumerate(pa.probes) if p.q in qs and p.basis == basis]
            if not cols:
                continue
            ms = (SZ.maximal(Z.coverable_subsets(cov, cols, n)) if n <= 12
                  else SZ.maximal(SZ.greedy_masks(cov, cols, n)))
            masks["abstract"] += [(m, basis, qs) for m in ms]
            if real(qs, basis == "X"):
                masks["placeable"] += [(m, basis, qs) for m in ms]
    out = dict(key=key, T2=n, n_embeddings=len(insts))
    for k, ms in masks.items():
        union = 0
        for m, _, _ in ms:
            union |= m
        one = any(m == full for m, _, _ in ms)
        two = one or any(a[0] | b[0] == full for i, a in enumerate(ms) for b in ms[i:])
        # greedy set cover size (upper bound on the flags needed in this model)
        left, k_ = full, 0
        while left and k_ < 4:
            best = max(ms, key=lambda x: bin(x[0] & left).count("1"), default=None)
            if best is None or not best[0] & left:
                break
            left &= ~best[0]
            k_ += 1
        out[k] = dict(options=len(ms), coverable_pairs=bin(union).count("1"), one_flag=one, two_flags=two,
                      greedy_cover=(k_ if not left else None))
    return out
EOF

input.content:
# RESULTS — search under the "continuing-data strict" readout rule

Run unattended on 2026-11-01, 6:50 pm – about 10:30 pm KST. Earlier results files are untouched; everything below is new.

## Answer (3 sentences)

**Yes: there are Willow double checks with fault distance 3 that also respect the readout rule when the data continue.** The search found 10, all with one ZZ flag plus one X flag on a one-root fold of depth 5; none existed with fold depth ≤ 4 (that part of the space was searched exhaustively). The best, `results/continuing/success02` (12 qubits, 24 CX), has 0 continuing-data conflicts, 0 strict violations and 0 malignant T configurations at ≤ 2 faults (350 at 3 faults); its T error per kept shot is 1 in 5,679,100 at uniform p = 0.1 % and 1 in 140,288 under the Willow calibration model, against 1 in 6,570,057 and 1 in 89,151 for success03 (7 conflicts) and 1 in 2,054,158 and 1 in 20,234 for G4 (2 conflicts).

**Naming.** To avoid a clash with the previous round's `results/zz/success03`, this report writes **cs00 … cs09** for `results/continuing/success00 … success09`. "success03" always means the old `results/zz/success03`.

## Status

| task | status | one line |
|---|---|---|
| Continuing-data check (reusable) | **PASS** | `constraints.continuing_data_violations` + `check_circuit(..., data_continue=True)` (`nnflags/constraints.py:301-341`, option at `:358`, `:404-405`); wrapper `continuing_data.strict_conflicts`. success03 = **7**, G4 (CX and native) = **2**, hand-made clean circuit = **0**, G4 with q7 unmeasured = 0 (tests). |
| 1. G6 analysis | **DONE** | Google keeps data and measured qubits on disjoint lines (data 9 / 11 / 13, measured 10 / 12) and **never reads out G6's q12**, the one ancilla on a data line (G4's q7). G6: 0 strict, 0 continuing-data conflicts in the cultivation stage. |
| 2. Search (`nnflags/search_continuing.py`) | **SUCCESS: 10 found, stopped** (stopping rule) | Stage 1 (depth ≤ 4, ≤ 12 qubits, 1 or 2 roots, exhaustive): 0. Deep pass (exact 2-cover + wider greedy, 539 best keys): 0, best 1 malignant pair. Stage 2 (depth ≤ 5, ≤ 13 qubits, 1 root; sampled, smallest first): 10 successes after 1,347 of 35,710 queued keys. Search wall time 2 h 10 min (< 4 h). |
| 3a. Uniform p = 0.1 % comparison | **DONE** | cs02 1 in 5,679,100 per kept shot; acceptance 89.28 % ± 0.010 % (rel. s.e. 0.011 %); 1.120 attempts per kept shot. |
| 3b. Realistic Willow noise | **DONE** | Calibration: cs02 1 in 140,288 vs success03 1 in 89,151 vs G4 1 in 20,234. Spec sheet: 1 in 363,150 / 360,080 / 90,830. |
| 3c. Google QVM E1 / E2 / E3 | **PASS** | E1: `willow_pink` validates the device circuit; round trip, flows and DEM identical. E2: 0 detector fires in 2,000 shots, fidelity 1 − 2.4 × 10⁻¹⁴ … see table (no e-notation in the tables). E3: 1,203 / 1,203 single events and 13,041 / 13,041 two-fault configurations agree with cliffordea; no kept corrupted state. |
| 3d. QVM E4 (noisy) | see E4 section | 4,000,000 shots of cs02 (≈ 11 min sampling, within the 30 min cap). |
| Figures (PNG only) | **DONE** | `figures/continuing_circuits.png`, `figures/continuing_comparison.png`. No PDF written. |
| Tests | see end | `nnflags/tests`, `qvm-google/tests`. |
| cliffordea untouched | see end | `git -C cliffordea status --porcelain --ignored`. |

**Settings of every number unless a line says otherwise:** distance 3; cultivated states T and S; `enum.noise.uniformly_depolarize` (cliffordea `enum/noise/main.py:9`) at p = 0.001; `FaultCombinator.get_kept_effects` (`enum/combinators/fault_combinator.py:236`) with `CliffordLogicalAnalyzer` via `nnflags.verify.verify` (`nnflags/verify.py:47-100`); T error per kept shot = cliffordea `error_rates_per_kept_shot` (`fault_combinator.py:164-225`) truncated at max_fault_count (mfc) 3; CX form; Willow 105-qubit grid; strict rule `live_rule="gate"`, `final_layer="auto"` (constraints.py defaults) **plus** the continuing-data rule.

## The rule as implemented

`constraints.continuing_data_violations(circuit, embedding, data_qubits=None)` (`nnflags/constraints.py:301`):
- data = MPP targets (cliffordea `find_data_indices`);
- for **every** TICK and every measurement of a non-data qubit (mid-check MRX of the root, final MX / M of ancillas and flags, anything else), one violation per data qubit on the same line r + c. Simultaneity does not exempt anything, since the data are not measured;
- a measured data qubit is reported as kind `data_measured`;
- `check_circuit(..., data_continue=True)` adds these to the strict check, which still runs unchanged (`constraints.py:404-405`).

Unit tests (`nnflags/tests/test_continuing.py`): success03 → 7 (same pairs as `continuing_data_conflicts`), G4-CX and G4-native → 2 (q7, line 19), a hand-made clean circuit → 0, G4 with q7 unmeasured → 0, G6 cultivation stage → 0, `data_measured` and the "simultaneous is not exempt" case, default `check_circuit` unchanged.

## 1. What Google's G6 does (`nnflags/g6_continuing.py`, `results/continuing_g6.json`)

G6 = Rosenfeld et al., arXiv:2512.13908, Fig. 4 "grafting N = 2 with cultivation" as run: 54 qubits, 124 TICKs, real Willow coordinates (`nnflags/data/google_circuits/rosenfeld2512_G6.stim`).

| item | G6 |
|---|---|
| cultivation data (targets of `I[T_gate]`, TICK 29) | 2 (4, 5), 4 (4, 7), 8 (5, 4), 10 (5, 6), 18 (6, 5), 20 (6, 7), 28 (7, 6) → **lines 9, 11, 13** |
| double-check ancillas | 3 (4, 6) line 10, 9 (5, 5) line 10, 11 (5, 7) line 12, 19 (6, 6) line 12, **12 (5, 8) line 13** |
| measurements in the cultivation stage | TICK 25: 3, 9, 11, 19; TICK 40 (mid check): 11, 19; TICK 55 (end of check): 3, 9, 11, 19 — all on lines 10, 12 |
| never measured | **q12**, on data line 13. It is only reset (TICK 56). Had it been read out with the others it would have hit data 20 (6, 7) and 28 (7, 6). |
| grafting | starts at TICK 57; first surface-code readout at TICK 90 |
| surface code after grafting | measure qubits on the **odd** lines 7–19, data on the **even** lines 8–18: disjoint by line parity. The cultivation data become surface-code measure qubits; the cultivation ancillas 3, 9, 11, 19 become surface-code data. |
| strict rule, whole G6 (gate rule; final layer auto or checked; data = cultivation data or none) | **0** |
| continuing-data rule on the cultivation stage (TICKs 0–56) | **0** |

**G4 ↔ G6.** G6's double check is G4's layout under a lattice symmetry. G4: data lines 15, 17, 19; ancillas 1, 4 on line 16, roots 6, 9 on line 18, **q7 on data line 19** — the source of G4's 2 continuing-data conflicts. In Fig. 2 (G4) the data are read out in the same final TICK, so measuring q7 is harmless there; in Fig. 4 (G6), where the data continue, Google drops exactly that measurement.

**Google's layout pattern.** (i) Data on one line parity, every measured qubit on the other (here: data odd, measured even). Since r + c changes by 1 along every coupler, this is the grid's checkerboard colouring, so every CZ joins a data line to a measured line. (ii) The parity roots of the mid check share one line with nothing else on it. (iii) An ancilla that has to sit on a data line is not read out (its detector is given up).

**What dropping q7 costs in cliffordea** (G4-CX with q7's M and detector removed = "G4 G6-style"): continuing 0, strict 0, equivalence ok; malignant T 0 / 0 / 7 / 667 at 0–3 faults (G4: 0 / 0 / 7 / 671); T error per kept shot 1 in 1,869,957 (G4: 1 in 2,054,158). Still fault distance 2.

**How this guided the search.** (a) Roles follow lines: the search labels every readout line D (data), M (measured) or R (root only) and grows trees only consistently with the labels. (b) Variant "U": an internal node on a D line may be an ancilla that is never read out (G6's q12 trick), at most one per base. (c) Two-root forests at diagonal neighbours on one line (G4 / G6 roots).

## 2. Search

### Search space and method (`nnflags/search_continuing.py`)

- **Bases** = fold forests in canonical CX form (`search_option1.build` / `to_circuit`): parity root(s) measured MRX mid-check, every node X-collects its children ASAP, unfold = time reverse, ancillas MX at the end; 7 data; leaves are data; internal nodes data or ancillas (also trees whose internal nodes are all ancillas).
- **Enumerated as embedded forests on Z², root at the origin, with a label per readout line** (D / M / R; `grow_pattern`, partitioned by line-label pattern and run in parallel). A qubit's role is its line's label, so the line-disjointness is a pruning rule during the growth. Extra pruning: ≤ 7 (+U) data-line nodes, ≤ n − 7 ancillas, every M node needs a child, remaining capacity must reach both ends of the line interval, ASAP fold depth ≤ dmax.
- **Deduplication** modulo translation and the 4 line-preserving symmetries (id, transpose, rot180, antitranspose); grouped by abstract key (`Base.canon` with roles D / A / U). **All embeddings of a key are kept** (cap 3,000; never reached in the flagged keys), because the line pattern of the flags depends on the placement.
- **Screen**: per key the best of the 210 code labellings (verify, mfc 2, T only). Keys with best malignant T count ≤ 12 go to the flag search.
- **Flags** (≤ 2): generalised Z / X flags of `zzflags` (probes, exact GF(2) prefilter, same verify / equivalence requirements as `search_zzflags`). Placement = some embedding of the key + free lattice points adjacent to all controls, **not on a data line**, not on a root line if live at the mid check, and the whole thing fits on Willow after a translation (`Placer`).
- **Two flag searches**: the greedy two-level search of `search_zzflags` (`process`), and a new exact **2-cover** (`process_cover`): every placeable (basis, control set) gets its maximal sets of base malignant pairs it separates; every two sets whose union is all pairs give a candidate pair of flags, built and verified together.
- **Success** = `check_circuit(..., data_continue=True) == []` at the saved Willow placement, `check_equivalence` ok (flags excluded from the reverse check), 0 malignant T at 1 and 2 faults; then verify at mfc 3.

### Why depth ≤ 4 failed and depth 5 works (evidence)

`results/continuing_cover_stats.json` (539 best one-root keys of s1, all labelled with their best labelling), `results/continuing_evidence.json`:

| question | abstract (any same-colour control set, no geometry) | placeable under the line rules |
|---|---|---|
| some single flag separates every base pair | 41 keys | 4 keys |
| two flags cover all base pairs (2-cover exists) | 356 keys | **86 keys** |
| some base pair cannot be separated by any placeable flag | — | 111 keys |
| greedy cover size 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / none | 41 / 262 / 236 / 0 / 0 | 4 / 58 / 327 / 39 / 111 |

- **The line rule, not the flags, is the obstruction.** Abstractly most good bases admit two covering flags; with flags forced off the data lines (and off the root line when live) only 86 do. A flag adjacent to a data qubit on line L must sit on L ± 1, which must be a measured line; with data on several lines this leaves few free points, and two-control flags need a point adjacent to both controls.
- **Flag faults.** For the 86 keys with a 2-cover the two flags are usually both Z flags, and the circuit then keeps 1 malignant pair made of a Z error on a Z flag (kicked back onto its control) and an X-type data error; only an X flag separates it, so 2 flags are not enough there.
- **Best at depth ≤ 4:** 1 malignant pair (28 keys in the deep pass). Example `results/continuing/attempt_1` (s1 key `A(D(),D(),D(A(A(D()),D())),D(A(D())))`, ZZ + X flag, 13 qubits): malignant T 0 / 0 / 1 / 429, T error per kept shot 1 in 6,785,004 (mfc 2), 1 in 3,594,228 (mfc 3), calibration model 1 in 73,562. Its surviving pair is X-type on both faults and a **third** Z flag could separate it (65 control sets abstractly, 3 placeable). So with depth ≤ 4 a third flag (not run) looks necessary; with depth 5 it is not.
- **Two-root forests** never screened below 13 malignant pairs (s1); one root is clearly better under this rule.
- **Depth 5 gives the checkerboard.** With the parity alternation data / measured on every coupler, a d = 3 fold that collects 7 data through measured ancillas only needs longer chains (root → data → ancilla → data), which costs one more fold layer. All 10 successes are of this kind; the G6-style unmeasured ancilla was never needed.

## Decisions made without the user

1. **Unmeasured ancillas allowed** (variant U, at most one per base), because Google's own G6 does exactly this with q12. They satisfy the rule as stated (a qubit that is never measured cannot dephase a line). All 10 successes turned out not to use it.
2. **Roles by line label.** In the all-measured variant a qubit's role is its line's role; this is the rule itself (a measured ancilla on a data line is a violation), not an extra restriction. Data internal nodes are allowed where their line is a data line.
3. **Reset is not a measurement**: resets do not dephase the readout line (as in all earlier rounds and in G6, which resets q12).
4. **Two-root forests only at diagonal neighbours on one line** (G4 / G6 root pattern); not enumerated at depth 5 because at depth ≤ 4 their best screen count was 13 malignant pairs vs 5 for one root.
5. **Screen threshold** T2 ≤ 12 for the flag search (successes of the ZZ round came from T2 10–11); the deep pass widened it to ≤ 14.
6. **Staged search** (s1 exhaustive, deep, s2 sampled by size) because the full depth-5 / 13-qubit / 2-root space did not fit in time or memory (s2 one-root alone: 9.5 M embeddings, 40 min to enumerate, 32 GB). Stage 2 stopped at the 10-success rule after 57 min; total search wall time 2 h 10 min.
7. **Exact 2-cover added** to the greedy search (deep pass, s2), with Z + X flag pairs tried first. 6 of the 10 successes were found by the greedy after the 2-cover (keys s2-00670 / 01348 / 01350, mode "cover+greedy"), 2 by the 2-cover itself (s2-00617).
8. **Best = lowest T error per kept shot at mfc 3, uniform noise** (rule of the task): cs02 (also 12 qubits, the smallest).
9. **G4 G6-style** (G4-CX without q7's measurement) added as a reference: it is the circuit Google actually runs in G6 and it is rule-compliant.
10. **E4** run with 4,000,000 shots for cs02 only; success03 and G4 E4 numbers are taken from `qvm-google/results/e4.json` (RESULTS_qvm.md), same noise model and protocol.
11. The new circuits are named cs00–cs09 in this report; the files keep the search's names `results/continuing/success00–09`.

## Open questions for the user

1. Is the **depth-5 fold** acceptable? It adds 2 TICKs to the base (cs02: 16 CX-form TICKs, 29 native, the same as success03), and under the calibration model it still wins.
2. Is the **G6 trick** (an ancilla that is never read out) acceptable in general? It was allowed here but not needed.
3. Should the **unsampled part of stage 2** (12–13-qubit and U bases at depth 5) be run, e.g. for a lower 3-fault count than cs02's 350 (success03 has 286)?
4. Should **resets** be treated as line-disturbing too? Google's G6 resets q12 next to data, so it seems not.
5. Distance 5 under this rule.

## The rule as implemented

`constraints.continuing_data_violations(circuit, embedding, data_qubits=None)` (`nnflags/constraints.py:301`):
- data = MPP targets (cliffordea `find_data_indices`);
- for **every** TICK and every measurement of a non-data qubit (mid-check MRX of the root, final MX / M of ancillas and flags, anything else), one violation per data qubit on the same line r + c. Simultaneity does not exempt anything, since the data are not measured;
- a measured data qubit is reported as kind `data_measured`;
- `check_circuit(..., data_continue=True)` adds these to the strict check, which still runs unchanged (`constraints.py:404-405`).

Unit tests (`nnflags/tests/test_continuing.py`): success03 → 7 (same pairs as `continuing_data_conflicts`), G4-CX and G4-native → 2 (q7, line 19), a hand-made clean circuit → 0, G4 with q7 unmeasured → 0, G6 cultivation stage → 0, `data_measured` and the "simultaneous is not exempt" case, default `check_circuit` unchanged.

## 1. What Google's G6 does (`nnflags/g6_continuing.py`, `results/continuing_g6.json`)

G6 = Rosenfeld et al., arXiv:2512.13908, Fig. 4 "grafting N = 2 with cultivation" as run: 54 qubits, 124 TICKs, real Willow coordinates (`nnflags/data/google_circuits/rosenfeld2512_G6.stim`).

| item | G6 |
|---|---|
| cultivation data (targets of `I[T_gate]`, TICK 29) | 2 (4, 5), 4 (4, 7), 8 (5, 4), 10 (5, 6), 18 (6, 5), 20 (6, 7), 28 (7, 6) → **lines 9, 11, 13** |
| double-check ancillas | 3 (4, 6) line 10, 9 (5, 5) line 10, 11 (5, 7) line 12, 19 (6, 6) line 12, **12 (5, 8) line 13** |
| measurements in the cultivation stage | TICK 25: 3, 9, 11, 19; TICK 40 (mid check): 11, 19; TICK 55 (end of check): 3, 9, 11, 19 — all on lines 10, 12 |
| never measured | **q12**, on data line 13. It is only reset (TICK 56). Had it been read out with the others it would have hit data 20 (6, 7) and 28 (7, 6). |
| grafting | starts at TICK 57; first surface-code readout at TICK 90 |
| surface code after grafting | measure qubits on the **odd** lines 7–19, data on the **even** lines 8–18: disjoint by line parity. The cultivation data become surface-code measure qubits; the cultivation ancillas 3, 9, 11, 19 become surface-code data. |
| strict rule, whole G6 (gate rule; final layer auto or checked; data = cultivation data or none) | **0** |
| continuing-data rule on the cultivation stage (TICKs 0–56) | **0** |

**G4 ↔ G6.** G6's double check is G4's layout under a lattice symmetry. G4: data lines 15, 17, 19; ancillas 1, 4 on line 16, roots 6, 9 on line 18, **q7 on data line 19** — the source of G4's 2 continuing-data conflicts. In Fig. 2 (G4) the data are read out in the same final TICK, so measuring q7 is harmless there; in Fig. 4 (G6), where the data continue, Google drops exactly that measurement.

**Google's layout pattern.** (i) Data on one line parity, every measured qubit on the other (here: data odd, measured even). Since r + c changes by 1 along every coupler, this is the grid's checkerboard colouring, so every CZ joins a data line to a measured line. (ii) The parity roots of the mid check share one line with nothing else on it. (iii) An ancilla that has to sit on a data line is not read out (its detector is given up).

**What dropping q7 costs in cliffordea** (G4-CX with q7's M and detector removed = "G4 G6-style"): continuing 0, strict 0, equivalence ok; malignant T 0 / 0 / 7 / 667 at 0–3 faults (G4: 0 / 0 / 7 / 671); T error per kept shot 1 in 1,869,957 (G4: 1 in 2,054,158). Still fault distance 2.

**How this guided the search.** (a) Roles follow lines: the search labels every readout line D (data), M (measured) or R (root only) and grows trees only consistently with the labels. (b) Variant "U": an internal node on a D line may be an ancilla that is never read out (G6's q12 trick), at most one per base. (c) Two-root forests at diagonal neighbours on one line (G4 / G6 roots).

## 2. Search

### Search space and method (`nnflags/search_continuing.py`)

- **Bases** = fold forests in canonical CX form (`search_option1.build` / `to_circuit`): parity root(s) measured MRX mid-check, every node X-collects its children ASAP, unfold = time reverse, ancillas MX at the end; 7 data; leaves are data; internal nodes data or ancillas (also trees whose internal nodes are all ancillas).
- **Enumerated as embedded forests on Z², root at the origin, with a label per readout line** (D / M / R; `grow_pattern`, partitioned by line-label pattern and run in parallel). A qubit's role is its line's label, so the line-disjointness is a pruning rule during the growth. Extra pruning: ≤ 7 (+U) data-line nodes, ≤ n − 7 ancillas, every M node needs a child, remaining capacity must reach both ends of the line interval, ASAP fold depth ≤ dmax.
- **Deduplication** modulo translation and the 4 line-preserving symmetries (id, transpose, rot180, antitranspose); grouped by abstract key (`Base.canon` with roles D / A / U). **All embeddings of a key are kept** (cap 3,000; never reached in the flagged keys), because the line pattern of the flags depends on the placement.
- **Screen**: per key the best of the 210 code labellings (verify, mfc 2, T only). Keys with best malignant T count ≤ 12 go to the flag search.
- **Flags** (≤ 2): generalised Z / X flags of `zzflags` (probes, exact GF(2) prefilter, same verify / equivalence requirements as `search_zzflags`). Placement = some embedding of the key + free lattice points adjacent to all controls, **not on a data line**, not on a root line if live at the mid check, and the whole thing fits on Willow after a translation (`Placer`).
- **Two flag searches**: the greedy two-level search of `search_zzflags` (`process`), and a new exact **2-cover** (`process_cover`): every placeable (basis, control set) gets its maximal sets of base malignant pairs it separates; every two sets whose union is all pairs give a candidate pair of flags, built and verified together.
- **Success** = `check_circuit(..., data_continue=True) == []` at the saved Willow placement, `check_equivalence` ok (flags excluded from the reverse check), 0 malignant T at 1 and 2 faults; then verify at mfc 3.

### Why depth ≤ 4 failed and depth 5 works (evidence)

`results/continuing_cover_stats.json` (539 best one-root keys of s1, all labelled with their best labelling), `results/continuing_evidence.json`:

| question | abstract (any same-colour control set, no geometry) | placeable under the line rules |
|---|---|---|
| some single flag separates every base pair | 41 keys | 4 keys |
| two flags cover all base pairs (2-cover exists) | 356 keys | **86 keys** |
| some base pair cannot be separated by any placeable flag | — | 111 keys |
| greedy cover size 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / none | 41 / 262 / 236 / 0 / 0 | 4 / 58 / 327 / 39 / 111 |

- **The line rule, not the flags, is the obstruction.** Abstractly most good bases admit two covering flags; with flags forced off the data lines (and off the root line when live) only 86 do. A flag adjacent to a data qubit on line L must sit on L ± 1, which must be a measured line; with data on several lines this leaves few free points, and two-control flags need a point adjacent to both controls.
- **Flag faults.** For the 86 keys with a 2-cover the two flags are usually both Z flags, and the circuit then keeps 1 malignant pair made of a Z error on a Z flag (kicked back onto its control) and an X-type data error; only an X flag separates it, so 2 flags are not enough there.
- **Best at depth ≤ 4:** 1 malignant pair (28 keys in the deep pass). Example `results/continuing/attempt_1` (s1 key `A(D(),D(),D(A(A(D()),D())),D(A(D())))`, ZZ + X flag, 13 qubits): malignant T 0 / 0 / 1 / 429, T error per kept shot 1 in 6,785,004 (mfc 2), 1 in 3,594,228 (mfc 3), calibration model 1 in 73,562. Its surviving pair is X-type on both faults and a **third** Z flag could separate it (65 control sets abstractly, 3 placeable). So with depth ≤ 4 a third flag (not run) looks necessary; with depth 5 it is not.
- **Two-root forests** never screened below 13 malignant pairs (s1); one root is clearly better under this rule.
- **Depth 5 gives the checkerboard.** With the parity alternation data / measured on every coupler, a d = 3 fold that collects 7 data through measured ancillas only needs longer chains (root → data → ancilla → data), which costs one more fold layer. All 10 successes are of this kind; the G6-style unmeasured ancilla was never needed.

## Decisions made without the user

1. **Unmeasured ancillas allowed** (variant U, at most one per base), because Google's own G6 does exactly this with q12. They satisfy the rule as stated (a qubit that is never measured cannot dephase a line). All 10 successes turned out not to use it.
2. **Roles by line label.** In the all-measured variant a qubit's role is its line's role; this is the rule itself (a measured ancilla on a data line is a violation), not an extra restriction. Data internal nodes are allowed where their line is a data line.
3. **Reset is not a measurement**: resets do not dephase the readout line (as in all earlier rounds and in G6, which resets q12).
4. **Two-root forests only at diagonal neighbours on one line** (G4 / G6 root pattern); not enumerated at depth 5 because at depth ≤ 4 their best screen count was 13 malignant pairs vs 5 for one root.
5. **Screen threshold** T2 ≤ 12 for the flag search (successes of the ZZ round came from T2 10–11); the deep pass widened it to ≤ 14.
6. **Staged search** (s1 exhaustive, deep, s2 sampled by size) because the full depth-5 / 13-qubit / 2-root space did not fit in time or memory (s2 one-root alone: 9.5 M embeddings, 40 min to enumerate, 32 GB). Stage 2 stopped at the 10-success rule after 57 min; total search wall time 2 h 10 min.
7. **Exact 2-cover added** to the greedy search (deep pass, s2), with Z + X flag pairs tried first. 6 of the 10 successes were found by the greedy after the 2-cover (keys s2-00670 / 01348 / 01350, mode "cover+greedy"), 2 by the 2-cover itself (s2-00617).

11. The new circuits are named cs00–cs09 in this report; the files keep the search's names `results/continuing/success00–09`.

## Open questions for the user

1. Is the **depth-5 fold** acceptable? It adds 2 TICKs to the base (cs02: 16 CX-form TICKs, 29 native, the same as success03), and under the calibration model it still wins.
2. Is the **G6 trick** (an ancilla that is never read out) acceptable in general? It was allowed here but not needed.

## The rule as implemented

`constraints.continuing_data_violations(circuit, embedding, data_qubits=None)` (`nnflags/constraints.py:301`):
- data = MPP targets (cliffordea `find_data_indices`);
- for **every** TICK and every measurement of a non-data qubit (mid-check MRX of the root, final MX / M of ancillas and flags, anything else), one violation per data qubit on the same line r + c. Simultaneity does not exempt anything, since the data are not measured;
